title: Shiffrin takes a more off-script approach in shifting focus beyond slalom and in Year 2 of podcast
summary: Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an "exploration season" in her 16th year on the World Cup circuit
story: Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an "exploration season" in her 16th year on the World Cup circuit
Mikaela Shiffrin is embracing an off-script approach in what the ski racer has dubbed her “exploration season.”

That includes on the mountain, where the three-time Olympic champion will prioritize training in giant slalom and super-G over her signature slalom event. It also extends to the microphone, with her plan to be even more free-flowing in interviews on her podcast, "What’s the Point.”
Just a way to feed her curiosity as she enters her 16th season on the World Cup circuit and second hosting her show. In her eyes, a speedy race and a seamless podcast have a common thread — cadence.

“When I’m skiing my best, it feels like a dance,” Shiffrin wrote in an email to The Associated Press as her 12-episode podcast kicked off Wednesday and featured media personality/fellow podcaster Kylie Kelce. "The turns link together and I stop thinking about them. A great episode has a similar rhythm. One question flows into the next, I might go ‘off script’ — it just feels natural and not forced. Then afterward the guest says something like, ‘That was such a fun conversation, let’s talk again soon.’ That’s my version of seeing green (signifying the fastest time) at the finish.”

From now until March, Shiffrin will feature episodes in which she interviews top names from around the sports world, including figure skater Ilia Malinin, rugby player Ilona Maher, tennis great Iga Swiatek and sportscaster Mike Tirico. The theme is what drives them toward success.
It’s a question she's pondered, too.

The six-time overall World Cup champion will focus her attention more on the GS and super-G this season. Sure, she will still compete in slalom, her top event. But she wanted to branch out after a season in which she won nine of 10 World Cup slalom events, along with capturing gold at the Milan Cortina Olympics.
A little bit of a scary decision, “because the safe choice was obvious,” the 31-year-old from Colorado said.

“I was coming off a successful slalom season, and if you only look at results, staying focused on slalom made the most sense,” she added. “But after 16 years on the World Cup, I felt a real curiosity pulling me toward GS and super-G, and I’ve learned to trust that feeling. Making peace with it came from being clear with myself about why I was doing it. It’s not about caring less or working less. It’s about recovering better, training with more intention, and racing slalom when I’m prepared for it. Slalom isn’t going anywhere.”

Shiffrin and her fellow racers push out of the start gate on Oct. 24 with a giant slalom competition in Soelden, Austria. Shiffrin said her first slalom race will be in Killington, Vermont, over Thanksgiving weekend.
“I’m keeping the door open,” Shiffrin said of her racing plans. "We’re calling this the exploration season, and I think that framing is what let me exhale.”
As for podcasting, she’s finding her groove. Last season, her guests included her fiancé, Norwegian ski racer Aleksander Aamodt Kilde, and gymnast Simone Biles, winner of seven Olympic gold medals.

“I learned that listening is a skill you train, just like skiing,” said Shiffrin, whose podcast launched in October 2025 in partnership with financial group Stifel. “In Season 1, I’d sometimes be so focused on getting to my next question that I’d miss the best thing a guest said. ... So in Year 2 I’m prepping less of a script and more of a direction. I also learned that I don’t need to be the expert in the room.”
Her plans going forward — and leading into the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps — remain fluid, in racing and podcasting.

“Whether I’m in the start gate, in the crowd cheering on former competitors and teammates, or even hosting live episodes of 'What’s the Point,’ I’ll tackle it with the same passion and curiosity I bring today," Shiffrin said. "What I can promise is that as long as I’m skiing, it’ll be because I want to, not because I feel I have to.”

title: Barcola's hat trick helps Liverpool rout LASK, Feyenoord fights back in Champions League
summary: Bradley Barcola has scored a hat trick and Liverpool has coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League
story: Bradley Barcola has scored a hat trick and Liverpool has coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League
LINZ, Austria -- Bradley Barcola scored a hat trick as Liverpool coasted to a 6-3 win at Austria’s LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday.
They were his first goals for the club since joining from European champion Paris Saint-Germain in the offseason.
Ronald Araújo also got his first Liverpool goal as he broke the deadlock with a header from a corner, less than two minutes before Barcola scored in the 24th from a lay-off by Lewis Koumas.
Ryan Gravenberch struck the post before Barcola got his second in the 37th, finishing with aplomb after being played through by Florian Wirtz.
Jeremie Frimpong, one of the smallest players on the field, headed Liverpool’s fourth in off the right post in the 51st.
Robert Ljubičić pulled a goal back in the 63rd, a minute after going on as a substitute, before Frimpong gave Barcola a simple tap-in to complete his hat trick in the 66th.
Koumas was left free to get Liverpool’s sixth six minutes later – it was the 21-year-old forward's first Liverpool goal.
But Florian Flecker – another LASK substitute – got the biggest cheer when he scored his team’s second with a diving header in the 74th, four minutes before he got another to complete the scoring.
Liverpool coach Andoni Iraola dropped Virgil van Dijk to the substitutes’ bench with French defender Jérémy Jacquet starting. The Dutch star replaced Jacquet for the last half hour or so.
Anis Hadj Moussa scored twice as Dutch leader Feyenoord came from behind to beat visiting Como 3-2 in the other early game.
Assane Diao gave Como the lead with the team’s first shot in the 18th minute after outmuscling Javi López on the right and firing inside the far post.
But Gjivai Zechiël replied two minutes later with a spectacular shot, and Algeria winger Hadj Moussa scored early in the second half before sealing the result in the 82nd.
Tasos Douvikas scored Como's consolation in stoppage time.
Scandal-hit Manchester City was hosting fellow big spender PSG later for its first European game since being charged with financial rule-breaking over nearly a decade in the Premier League.

Also later, Real Madrid was visiting Roma for coach José Mourinho’s return, Bodø/Glimt was playing Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis was entertaining Porto, Fenerbahçe was visiting Aston Villa, Stuttgart traveled to Slovan Bratislava, and Ukraine’s Shakhtar Donetsk was hosting AEK Athens at Chelsea’s ground in London.

title: Shai Hope’s 102 gives West Indies series-leveling win over India in fourth cricket T20
summary: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
story: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
HYDERABAD, India -- Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2.
Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl.
It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.
In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs.
Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s.
Bengaluru will host the deciding T20 on Saturday.
Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). Axar Patel trapped Andrew lbw in the fifth over but West Indies still got 79-1 in the powerplay.
Hope then added another 58 off 24 balls with Shimron Hetmyer, reaching 50 off 28 balls with the help of five sixes. He sped to a second hundred in the series with another four sixes.
Hope also became only the fifth batter to score multiple hundreds in a bilateral T20 series. Overall, it was his fourth hundred in seven innings across ODIs and T20s on this tour.
He wasn’t finished, despite Prince Yadav sending back Hetmyer for 33, while Rovman Powell scored 24.
Sherfane Rutherford scored 49 not out off 26 balls to provide the final flourish, hitting four fours and three sixes, as West Indies breached 200.

Hope and Rutherford added 91 off only 43 balls, as India served a slow over-rate penalty in the final over. Nitish Reddy gave away 19 runs in the 20th, with Hope reaching his century with a six off the last ball.
In reply, Samson hit four sixes to give India a quick start. He and Abhishek Sharma (29) added 60 off 25 balls as India scored 80-2 in the powerplay.
Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over – Samson was out caught at square leg on the first ball and then three balls later, Ishan Kishan was caught at deep mid wicket for six.
India also lost skipper Shreyas Iyer (16) before the halfway mark, and was down to 97-3.
Abhishek Sharma didn’t get going, scoring 29 off 24 balls, with three fours and a six. His dismissal was the turning point – he was caught off Gudakesh Motie at long off in the 12th over.
Motie also had Naman Dhir stumped for a golden duck.
Tilak Varma fought hard with 43 off 25 balls along with Nitish Reddy’s cameo (41 off 20 balls) but it went in vain.
Paul picked three wickets in the 19th over to wrap up the innings.

title: Matchup between 3 elite receivers could overshadow QBs when No. 4 Ohio St. takes on No. 5 Indiana
summary: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend
story: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend
Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith seems to break records every weekend.
Indiana receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are etching their names into Indiana lore on a weekly basis, too.

On Saturday, those three — all ranked among the top four receiver prospects in April's NFL draft — will share the field for the eagerly anticipated Big Ten championship game rematch between the fourth-ranked Buckeyes and defending national champion and fifth-ranked Hoosiers.
This dream matchup for pro scouts turns into an absolute nightmare for defensive coordinators, secondaries and even, yes, two-time Associated Press Coach of the Year Curt Cignetti.

“He (Smith) has taken it up a notch without question, I think he has nine touchdown catches in the last three or four games," Cignetti said Monday. “There is no one like him right now playing at this level. We've got two really good ones, but he (Smith) is a freak. We’re going to have to do a great job on him.”
Typically, in these high-stakes matchups, quarterbacks become the feature attractions. Josh Hoover and Julian Sayin certainly have done their part.
Hoover arrived at Indiana this season from TCU with a reputation for turning the ball over and with the tough job of replacing Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza.

So far, he's been up to the task. He ranks second in the Football Bowl Subdivision in passing efficiency (200.52), is tied for third in TD passes (17) and has not thrown an interception while helping Indiana (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) extend the FBS' longest active winning streak to 22.

Sayin has nearly matched Hoover's stat line, ranking fourth in efficiency (194.45) with 17 TD passes, though he drew the ire of coach Ryan Day last week when he threw his second interception of the season and lost a fumble in the Buckeyes' victory over Maryland.
But what makes these two offenses really click are strong ground games and elite receivers.

Smith already owns Ohio State's career marks for receptions, yards receiving and TD catches and ranks second nationally this season with 48 catches, 916 yards and 11 TDs. He opened conference play with back-to-back games of double-digit catches and 200-plus yards and has shown he wants to succeed Mendoza as this year's Heisman winner.

“I didn't know I had that much (yardage),” Smith said when asked about celebrating more regularly with the Heisman pose. “But, yeah, just got to keep (reminding) Heisman voters or whoever it is, the best player in the country is right here.”

Smith also had a big game when these teams last met in December — eight receptions for 144 yards — but he did not score. Keeping him out of the end zone will be an all hands on deck assignment for Indiana.
It won't be any easier for the Buckeyes (5-1, 3-0).

Becker, who has a propensity for nabbing jump balls, played a key role in the Hoosiers' title run, including his six-catch, 126-yard performance against Ohio State last December. His acrobatic 33-yard catch on third-and-6 with 2:26 left essentially sealed Indiana’s 13-10 victory over the Buckeyes in the Big Ten championship game.
This season, he and Marsh form one of the nation's most dangerous pass-catching duos.
Marsh's first immersion into the “Indiana way” was when Cignetti ripped him for showing up to the first day of spring practice in gold shoes and then talked about it publicly.

Lately, though, the record-breaking transfer from Michigan State has earned his keep. His biggest game of the season came last week when he had six receptions for 147 yards and TD catches of 75 and 44 yards in the fourth quarter that gave Indiana a 20-17 come-from-behind win at Nebraska.

“Nick did a great job running the route and I put it on him,” Hoover said when asked about the 75-yard score. “He caught it and did something with it, so it just shows you what our guys are able to do when we get the ball in their hands. I've got to continue to find ways to get these guys the ball, let them do their thing.”
That's exactly what Day wants to prevent from a duo that has combined for 59 receptions, 1,057 yards and 14 TDs. Becker has one more catch, one more yard and two more scores than Marsh.
But Day has seen just how good they are together.

“These guys, in particular, are very clean route runners, play really strong on contact, have really good body control,” Day said. “They have a run-after-catch ability. (They're) very, very confident playing man-to-man coverage, do an excellent job with their slants and fades and back shoulder fades. You can tell that's clearly taught at a very high level there.”
Both also pride themselves in downfield blocking, a must for a team coached by a former receivers coach. Becker has returned punts this season too.

Just don't expect this weekend's only top five matchup to be a track meet. It's going to be physical and action-packed with big plays, big disappointments and three highly touted receivers trying to gain the upper hand against defenses tracking their every move.
It won't be easy, but it promises to be worth watching.

“Just his explosive playmaking ability,” Indiana linebacker Isaiah Jones said when asked what he's seen from Smith. “Whether it's a quadruple move down the middle of the field or they're going to turn him a screen, he can turn it on like that and start getting vertical. But I think the thing that's really impressed us is that he's not just this vertical threat that's like a track star. He'll catch the ball in space and start getting vertical from like low drags and stuff like that.”

title: Angel Reese caps tumultuous journey, takes center stage with the Dream in the WNBA Finals
summary: Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA’s brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship
story: Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA’s brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship
Angel Reese is the biggest star left on the WNBA's brightest stage as she gets her first chance at winning a pro championship.

It’s been a tumultuous journey but coming to Atlanta this season has been the perfect move for the three-time All-Star, whose accomplishments this year have quieted many of her critics. Leading the Dream to the franchise's first title would silence the rest of them. That quest begins Saturday when the best-of-seven series against the Golden State Valkyries opens in California.

Reese is the first player from the heralded 2024 draft class that saw Caitlin Clark go No. 1 to reach the finals as a starter. The 6-foot-3 Reese went seventh in that draft to the Chicago Sky and has used that to fuel her to become one of the top players in the league — winning the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year award this season.

“I think it was important for me to go through what I went through,” Reese said of falling to seventh in the draft. “Being able to build character, going through adversity drove character and I was able to learn from a lot of things, being able to continue to be great, but also learning to know that I can be better.”

Her first two seasons ended early, not just by missing the playoffs, but also because of injuries. She had wrist surgery at the end of her rookie year and had a back issue last year. Despite leading the WNBA in rebounding each of her first three seasons, averaging a double-double every year, critics questioned her offensive efficiency.

Online keyboard warriors came up with the phrase “mebounds" to call attention to Reese grabbing her own misses. Reese, who has her own custom Barbie doll, turned that into a positive. She created a business initiative and donated some of the proceeds to her foundation to combat cyber bullying.

“One thing that always set Angel apart as a rookie was her tenacity, her desire," NBC analyst Cheryl Miller said. "I think she’s one of those players who feels like the more you tell her who she’s not and try to set limits, she’s going to break those feelings every time.”

Reese has already matched Breanna Stewart and A'ja Wilson. Those WNBA icons also reached the finals in their third season in the league. Reese will try to follow Stewart and win the title in her first try.

Reese didn't make the playoffs in her first two years in the league when she played with Chicago. Atlanta general manager Dan Padover said the night his team lost to Clark and the Indiana Fever in the playoffs last season that he decided he needed to acquire Reese. She was the missing piece that the franchise needed to get back to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. So he did just that, trading for Reese.

“Coming to Atlanta, obviously the goal for me was just to get them past the first round, because I wanted that for them," Reese said. “I watched them last year when they played how they came up short, and we saw the film from the beginning of the season."

Reese said that coach Karl Smesko still played those clips from when they lost in the first round. She didn’t make the postseason in her two years in Chicago. She just wanted to get a chance to play in the playoffs, and after helping Atlanta knock off Washington and New York, she has the Dream in the championship round.

“I think the expectations for me have risen beyond what I expected,” she said. “Obviously I didn’t know we were going to be going to the finals, but obviously now the expectation is being in the finals every single year. Being here with the Dream, it just makes it a lot of fun. They pour into you, the organization is great, so I really love it.”
Reese has drawn high praise from Golden State coach Natalie Nakase, who worked with her at the World Cup.

“Yeah, she’s an ultimate, ultra competitor,” Nakase said. “To me, when we were at USA, you heard her voice constantly. So when she didn’t start, you heard her. She was constantly cheering her teammates on when they needed to. She constantly called them out when we needed energy."
Nakase said Reese's competitive edge is a huge reason Atlanta is in the finals, and she knows Reese "is not going to let any possession slip.”

Reese is no stranger to winning championships. She helped LSU win the NCAA title her junior year, beating Clark and Iowa in the title game that had over 18 million people watch on television. She also was on the U.S. national team that won a fifth straight World Cup last month.

“All of them are just like win or go home situations for me," Reese said of her college experience. "That’s kind of the mindset how it’s always been. Every game I’m treating it like it’s win or go home, and making sure I put my body out there every single night and give it my all, every little detail.

“We always talk about the value of one, that’s Karl’s big emphasis,” Reese said. "The value of one, the value of one, one rebound, one box out, one shot, one free throw, making sure I am perfecting and doing everything right. That’s kind of been the mindset for me.”
AP Sports Writer Janie McCauley and freelance writer Alan Cole in Atlanta contributed to this report.

title: Bills-Rams shootout, 49ers-Seahawks turnover fest highlight the Week 5 slate
summary: The two most consequential games in Week 5 were tight high-scoring affairs between Super Bowl contenders that weren't decided until the end
story: The two most consequential games in Week 5 were tight high-scoring affairs between Super Bowl contenders that weren't decided until the end
The two most consequential games in Week 5 were tight, high-scoring affairs between Super Bowl contenders that weren't decided until the last seconds.
How they got there couldn't be more different.
The Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 in overtime in a back-and-forth game that featured noteworthy performances from the last two AP NFL MVPs in Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford.
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a turnover-filled battle where the defenses fueled much of the scoring.
Let's start with the Bills win on Monday night that was the latest shootout that Allen pulled out with a historic dual-threat performance.

Allen ran 10 times for 121 yards and a touchdown and also threw for 210 yards and a score for his fourth career game with at least 100 yards rushing and 200 yards passing. That's the second-most ever but he has a long way to catch the leader with Lamar Jackson having nine of them so far.

Allen did become the first player in NFL history to average both 10 yards per rush and 10 yards per pass in a game with at least 10 attempts of both and extended a remarkable winning streak for Buffalo. The Bills have won eight straight regular-season games when allowing at least 31 points. No other team in NFL history has had a streak longer than four with Baltimore doing that in 2023-24 and Green Bay in the 2011 season.

Stafford and the Rams were on the other side of the odd history, somehow losing a game when they gained 454 yards, had five touchdowns from scrimmage, 33 first downs and didn't turn the ball over once. They became just the second team in the Super Bowl era to hit those marks in a loss. Pittsburgh did it in a 42-37 loss to Kansas City in Week 2 of the 2018 season.

Stafford threw for 383 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions and now has four games since the start of last season when he threw for at least 370 yards with three TDs and no interceptions in a loss in the regular season or playoffs.
No one else has done that even once in the past two seasons or has more four of those games in their careers.
The 49ers-Seahawks game was known more for the mistakes than the stellar offensive play with the seven combined turnovers the most in any game this season.
The offenses also struggled to move the ball for most of the game, outside of one go-ahead touchdown drive by the 49ers in the fourth quarter, as the teams combined to average 4.48 yards per play.

But despite all that, there were plenty of points as San Francisco won 32-29. This was the first game since at least 2000 with four touchdown drives that started inside the opponent’s 25 with all four coming after takeaways. The Niners also recovered a fumble in the end zone for a fifth touchdown.

That helped make this the first game in 10 years with at least 60 points and teams averaging less than 4.5 yards per play. It last happened in Week 4 of the 2016 season when New Orleans beat San Diego 35-34 in a game that had an average of 4.47 yards per play.
Players picked in the top five of the draft typically have a long leash to prove they can produce.
Marvin Harrison Jr. is the rare top-five player that a team cut ties on before the end of his third season.

Arizona traded Harrison to Houston after drafting him fourth overall in 2024. Harrison played just 33 games for the Cardinals before being dealt with a seventh-round pick for a second and a sixth next year. Harrison had only five catches this season and just 1,578 yards receiving in his career with Arizona.

Only eight players taken in the top five since 2000 played fewer games for their original team. The list includes notable draft busts like JaMarcus Russell (31 games), Jason Smith (29), Dion Jordan (26), Jeff Okudah (25), Justin Blackmon (20) and Charles Rogers (15).

Trent Richardson, the third pick in 2012, was dealt by Cleveland to Indianapolis after 17 games played, and Trey Lance was traded by San Francisco to Dallas after appearing in eight games as the third overall pick by the 49ers in 2021.

Two other players who played more than 33 games for their first team also were dealt before the end of year three with Seattle trading 2009 No. 4 pick Aaron Curry to the Raiders in his third season and Tampa Bay trading 2007 No. 4 pick Gaines Adams to Chicago in his third season.
Jared Goff is off to a record-breaking start this season for the Detroit Lions.

After throwing three touchdown passes in a 45-21 win over Arizona on Sunday, Goff became the first quarterback in NFL history with at least 12 touchdown passes and no turnovers in the first five games.

Russell Wilson had 12 touchdown passes and no interceptions to start the 2019 season but lost a fumble. Two other players in the last decade had 11 touchdown passes and no turnovers in the first five games, with Drew Brees doing it in 2018 and Alex Smith in 2017.
No other quarterback this season has more than four TD passes without a turnover with backups Drew Lock and Marcus Mariota pulling that off.
Calais Campbell took over sole possession of most games played by a defensive lineman when the 40-year-old played 32 snaps in Baltimore's overtime win at Atlanta.

Campbell has now played in 283 games in a career that began with Arizona in 2008. He passed Jim Marshall for the most games played by a defensive lineman. The only defender with more career games is Hall of Fame cornerback Darrell Green with 295 — a mark Campbell could tie if he plays in every regular-season game this season.
If he does that, he would trail only Jerry Rice (303 games) and Bruce Matthews (296) for the most games played by a non-quarterback or specialist.

title: US Soccer plans new national women's club competition
summary: The U.S. Soccer federation plans a new national women’s club competition that will involve teams from the National Women’s Soccer League and the Gainbridge Super League
story: The U.S. Soccer federation plans a new national women’s club competition that will involve teams from the National Women’s Soccer League and the Gainbridge Super League

CHESTER, Pa. -- The U.S. Soccer federation announced Wednesday it plans a new national women's club competition that will include teams from the National Women's Soccer League and the Gainbridge Super League.

There is no launch date yet for the Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup, which will have a prize pool of $1.5 million. The single-elimination competition will serve as a national championship and a pathway to qualification for the CONCACAF W Champions Cup.

“We’re working very closely with both the NWSL and the Gainbridge Super League to figure out what is the optimal time to do this,” U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said. “Obviously, we want to put it into play as soon as possible, but we also want to be respectful of each league’s calendar and how do we best go forth and do this. And I’ve got to say, I’ve been very impressed with both leagues and how much they’re leaning in and collaborating and cooperating to make this happen.”
Parlow Cone said the competition could be open to other clubs, including amateur teams, much like the men's U.S. Open Cup.

“We’re looking at the option for lower division professional teams being able to join, as well as amateur women’s teams being able to join, and what that could and should look like, but we’re also not of the thought that the tournament can’t evolve. So maybe we start with the NWSL and GSL, and then evolve and engage the other teams,” she said. “We’re announcing this in real time as we are still trying to put all the pieces together."

The growth of women's soccer has spurred club competitions in recent years. Internationally, the women's Champions Cup is in its second year, and the FIFA Women's Club World Cup is set to start in 2028.

The aim of Crest Cup is to capitalize on the popularity of the game, which is expected to grow with the World Cup next summer in Brazil. The United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica have a joint bid for the 2031 tournament.
The tournament also aims to give high-level, meaningful competition for club teams, while spurring player development.

“As we gear up for the World Cup in 2031, I think this is a great timing in order to create another competition, because most of the the players and the coaches and the teams in our ecosystem, they only get that international exposure if they make their national teams, or if they’re lucky, one or two teams to be able to play in the CONCACAF tournament. But this is another way to get more players interleague competition that could then lead to international competition in really meaningful games,” Parlow Cone said.

Blank has long been a supporter of U.S. Soccer. The federation recently opened the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center in Lafayette, Georgia. Blank owns Major League Soccer's Atlanta United and and an expansion NWSL team, Atlanta City FC, set to start play in 2028.

title: Connor McDavid's 3-point first period propels Oilers past winless LA Kings 4-1 for 5th straight win
summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists in the dynamic first period of his four-point night, propelling the Edmonton Oilers to a 4-1 victory over the winless Los Angeles Kings
story: Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists in the dynamic first period of his four-point night, propelling the Edmonton Oilers to a 4-1 victory over the winless Los Angeles Kings

LOS ANGELES -- Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists in the dynamic first period of his four-point night, propelling the Edmonton Oilers to a 4-1 victory over the winless Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday.

Vasily Podkolzin got his sixth and seventh goals of the season, Leon Draisaitl also scored and Devon Levi made 39 saves for the Oilers, who have won five straight and scored at least three goals in every game of their 5-0-1 start.

McDavid recorded at least three points in a period for the 33rd time in his 11-year career, doing it in the first period for the 10th time. The six-time Art Ross Trophy winner as the NHL's top scorer has a whopping 16 points already this season with five multi-point games.

Brandt Clarke scored for the Kings, who dropped to 0-3-2 to begin coach Peter Laviolette's first season despite outshooting the Oilers 40-16. The Kings are still adjusting to their new direction under Laviolette, who wants offensive aggression from a team that has played deliberate, defense-first hockey for nearly two decades.
Los Angeles and Philadelphia are the NHL's only winless teams.
Evan Bouchard had two assists for the Oilers, who are off to their strong start despite playing without injured Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins.

Edmonton opened the scoring when McDavid froze Cody Ceci and fed the puck low to the quick-wristed Draisaitl. One minute later, Podkolzin converted the rebound after McDavid blew past Mikey Anderson and blistered a shot off Darcy Kuemper.

After the Kings had pinned Edmonton in its own end for nearly two full shifts late in the first period, McDavid came off the bench, accepted Ty Emberson's pass at the blue line in stride and scored his fourth goal.
Kuemper was replaced by Anton Forsberg to start the second.
Clarke scored late in the second period on a long shot through traffic. The goal was Clarke's first since Los Angeles' young defensive cornerstone inked a five-year, $37 million deal last June.
McDavid and Draisaitl assisted on Podkolzin's empty-net goal.
Oilers: Host Utah on Thursday.
Kings: Host Boston on Saturday.

title: Kraken beat Flyers 3-2 in shootout as Philadelphia’s winless start reaches 8 games
summary: Bobby McMann scored a goal in regulation and then added the game-winner in the fifth round of the shootout as the Seattle Kraken beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 on Tuesday night
story: Bobby McMann scored a goal in regulation and then added the game-winner in the fifth round of the shootout as the Seattle Kraken beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 on Tuesday night
PHILADELPHIA -- Bobby McMann scored a goal in regulation and then added the game-winner in the fifth round of the shootout as the Seattle Kraken beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 on Tuesday night.
The loss extended Philadelphia's franchise record for a winless streak to start a season to eight games (0-5-3).

McMann scored his third goal of the season on the power play in the first period when a loose puck bounced to him in the right circle, and he snapped a shot past Philadelphia goalie Dan Vladar. He later beat Vladar in the shootout after Vladar made several nice stops to keep the Flyers' hopes alive.
Ville Ottavainen scored his first NHL goal at 8:54 of the second period after the Flyers got caught with tired players on the ice following an icing call on defenseman David Jiricek.
Philipp Grubauer made 24 saves to earn the win for Seattle, which has won three straight road games.

Grubauer got into it with Flyers forward Trevor Zegras on two successive plays in the second period. Zegras slashed Grubauer, and Grubauer responded with a cross-check. After Zegras came out of the box, Grubauer threw a puck at him; Zegras shot it back at him after the whistle, and they got into a skirmish again, and both were penalized.
Zegras beat Grubauer with a third-period goal as the Flyers evened the score with two goals. Grubauer got the better of Zegras, though, stoning him in the shootout.
Christian Dvorak also scored for Philadelphia and Vladar made 29 saves in defeat.
Kraken: Continue their five-game road trip Thursday at Tampa Bay.
Flyers: Travel to Detroit on Thursday.

title: Jimmy Butler, Paul George, James Harden among All-Stars failed to win a title in Philly. Can LeBron?
summary: The 76ers have made numerous attempts to find the missing piece to win a championship with Joel Embiid
story: The 76ers have made numerous attempts to find the missing piece to win a championship with Joel Embiid

PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers tried. Oh, how they tried, to find that missing All-Star, that missing piece they could team with Joel Embiid and a rotating cast of starters and could finally lead the franchise to an NBA championship.
Jimmy Butler. Paul George. James Harden. Tobias Harris. Al Horford.
Nothing more now in Philly than throwback jerseys in the back of some teenager's closet.

Josh Harris bought the team in 2011 and not even a year later the Sixers made the first splash of his tenure with a blockbuster deal when they landed All-Star big man Andrew Bynum in a trade with the Lakers.

Bynum with his achy knees never played a game with the Sixers. Butler, Harden and most of the rest certainly had their moments, yet they not only failed to win a championship in Philadelphia, but they also could not get the Sixers even out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
That doesn't even count the draft night disappointments since Harris' first draft in 2012. Ben Simmons. Jahlil Okafor. Markelle Fultz. Michael Carter-Williams.
The trade-deadline blockbusters and late-night deals all seemed at the time like the Sixers were swinging for the fences.
The moves were just bunts compared to the summer of 2026.

The Sixers are as all-in as they've ever been in playing for a championship after they traded for Jaylen Brown, an NBA Finals MVP and champion with the Boston Celtics, and landed LeBron James as a free agent on the NBA veteran minimum salary.
If it doesn't work now, with perhaps the best starting five in the NBA, when will it for the Sixers?
“I wouldn't say it didn't work out,” Embiid said of the second-fiddle failures. “Obviously, we didn't win. It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe.”

The 76ers only have to look at their last championship in 1983 to know that sometimes going outside the organization is the right call. Take 1982, when the Sixers signed reigning NBA MVP Moses Malone to a six-year free-agent contact. Malone won MVP honors again in his first season with the Sixers and helped lead stalwarts Julius Erving, Maurice Cheeks, Bobby Jones and Andrew Toney to an NBA title in 1983.
Brown and James will try to do the same in Year 1 and avoid joining this recent list of stars who left Philadelphia without a ring:

Former Sixer executive Daryl Morey had his heart set on Harden and landed the feared Beard from Brooklyn at the February 2022 trade deadline. He had been one of the league’s top players for the previous decade, having won three scoring titles and the 2018 league MVP award.
Harden essentially forced his way with trades out of Houston and Brooklyn and soon added the Sixers to the list.

His low moments with the 76ers came in the 2023 playoffs when the Sixers blew a 3-2 lead to the Celtics. Harden was 0 for 6 on 3s in Game 2 and Game 6 losses. He scored only nine points in Game 7, and he went scoreless in the second half.
Harden got into a contractual dispute in the offseason that lingered into training camp, and he was traded in October 2023 to the Los Angeles Clippers.

The Sixers made another deadline deal in 2019 to land Harris from the Clippers. Harris had a modest career, and the Sixers were already his fifth NBA team at the time of the deal. Feeling the pressure to keep Harris after trading away a slew of draft picks, the Sixers signed him to a five-year, $180 million contract that summer.

Harris never made an All-Star team over those five years, and he never delivered in playoff crunch time. His low moment came in a 2024 playoff loss to the Knicks. Harris, who averaged 17 points in the regular season, went scoreless in 29 minutes for the Sixers in a Game 6 loss that ended their season.

George was indeed the chosen one for the Sixers in the summer of 2024. He signed a four-year, $212 million free-agent contract after the nine-time All-Star spurned the Los Angeles Clippers. With the move — and a coinciding extension with All-Star Tyrese Maxey — the franchise was feeling like they had assembled a championship-level Big Three.

George's low moment in Philadelphia was a 25-game suspension last season for flunking a drug test that put a permanent blemish on his career. George returned to have a solid postseason for the Sixers against the Celtics, which may have been his greatest contribution.
The deal wasn't a total loss. The Sixers were able to use George as the offseason anchor in a trade with the Celtics to obtain Brown.
Butler was an exciting arrival for the Sixers in November 2018 when they got a four-time All-Star in a trade with Minnesota.
Butler, Embiid and Simmons were christened a Big Three — one of many attempted by the Sixers over the last 15 years — and the team was instantly considered a serious threat to win it all.

Butler finished the season with the Sixers before going to Miami. Butler was frustrated with the Sixers' organizational structure and clashed with former coach Brett Brown. Butler felt he needed the ball in his hands and was irked in the playoffs — when the Sixers lost a semifinal series to Toronto in seven games — when he switched primary playmaking roles with Simmons.
His moment in Philadelphia actually came in 2022 when he returned with the Heat. After Miami eliminated the Sixers in the playoffs, Butler yelled as he walked off the court, “Tobias Harris over me?!"
Honorable mentions to Horford, Bynum — whose wasted season kickstarted the rebuild known as “The Process” — Danny Green, Josh Richardson and, well, the list goes on.
The 76ers hope the list of fiascos ends with James and Brown — and with a parade down Broad Street.

title: A wall of screens, 32 teams and 1 mission: How NHL Player Safety tracks trouble in real time
summary: The NHL's Player Safety room in Manhattan is buzzing with activity, especially on busy nights when all 32 teams are in action
story: The NHL's Player Safety room in Manhattan is buzzing with activity, especially on busy nights when all 32 teams are in action
NEW YORK -- The puck dropped just after 6 p.m. in Detroit, and the hum of activity had long been underway inside the NHL Player Safety room at league headquarters in Manhattan.

Someone was assigned to every game, and this was the busiest night of the season so far with all 32 teams in action. The room is a hockey lover's paradise with five giant television screens and more than a dozen other monitors showing every single goal, save, hit, penalty, injury and more.
The watchers who work there like to say they see everything. And they have an important job to do.

This is the first line of defense for head injuries, with a vast majority of the communication coming as calls to concussion spotters monitoring for the need to pull players off the ice for evaluation. It is also the beginning of the process to determine supplemental discipline, with an intricate process of watching, vetting, logging and reporting questionable plays to determine potential suspensions and fines long before George Parros hands them down and video explanations come out.
General managers, coaches and players are welcome to visit. The department was established in 2011.

“For the most part, when people come in, they do leave with knowing at least one thing: We definitely saw what you think that we should see,” said Damian Echevarrieta, the NHL's senior vice president of player safety. “Now, you might not always agree with our decisions, but the fact that we are on top of it and notice every single incident of every game, I think people really leave here knowing that.”
The Associated Press sat in Tuesday night to see how it all goes down.

With 16 games going as part of ESPN's “Frozen Frenzy,” there are concussion spotters seated at the front of the control room. It is the responsibility of, on this night, eight game-watchers to first alert a spotter of any possible contact to the head. Spotters then have a direct line to reach team medical staffs at games.

The first call comes at 6:33 p.m. to look at New Jersey's Jack Hughes high-sticking Detroit's Keegan Kolesar. It's quickly cleared of being a spotter concern, but Echevarrieta wants the video clipped just in case for later.
Just after 7 p.m., spotters are made aware of Florida's Lars Eller taking a puck to the face in the first period at Columbus and leaving the ice to get stitched up.

Later, it's Montreal's Noah Dobson, and there is chatter throughout the night as they keep an eye on him for any visible signs of a concussion. Game-watchers have access to Hawk-Eye camera angles from each end of the ice, along with a full-rink view from high above and the ability to isolate on a single player.
Another task is making sure all players required to wear helmets in warmups are doing so, along with mandatory neck guards for first-year players.

Anyone doing a rookie lap, like Anaheim's Roger McQueen on Tuesday night, gets a grace period — but when he was still helmetless several minutes later, Player Safety was ready to call the arena. McQueen had his helmet on two minutes later.

At 7:52 p.m., Panthers defenseman Uvis Balinskis was down on the ice and replays show Blue Jackets forward Mathieu Olivier spearing his opponent in the groin. Echevarrieta and Co. clock it before officials review the video and eject Olivier with a game misconduct for slashing.

Any time there is the potential for further punishment, a report catalogs what happened, if there was a penalty called, the players involved, any disciplinary history, the aggressor's next game and video clips of the incident. That report is sent to the entire department.

When Parros, a retired enforcer who took over player safety decisions in 2017, deems something worthy of a possible review, he emails Echevarrieta and the rest of the room for thoughts to be shared just with him. Parros asked by 8:17 p.m., less than a half-hour after the play unfolded.
On Wednesday, Olivier was fined $5,000, the maximum allowed under the collective bargaining agreement. A suspension was determined not to be warranted in part because he had no disciplinary history.

Seattle goaltender Philipp Grubauer shoving Philadelphia's Trevor Zegras raised attention around the room not long after. That was more to have video evidence of a goalie roughing penalty for future reference.

Echevarrieta has been with the NHL since 1999, working in hockey operations in Toronto under Colin Campbell. That is still where the situation room does the same daily monitoring — but for goal reviews to determine if the puck is over the goal line and to assist with coach's challenges.
A decade and a half ago came the opportunity to copy many of the same procedures to use in Player Safety.
“It was already a time-tested system that we put into place, and it’s worked really well,” Echevarrieta said.

Repetition over the years has helped, he said, to where now even the most chaotic nights like Tuesday run smoothly. Interspersed in the job responsibilities is plenty of hockey talk — Matthew Tkachuk assisting on brother Brady's natural hat trick, and the few-seconds spoiler — “(Alexis) Lafrenière scored again!”

At multiple points, 10 games were going on at the same time, with Echevarrieta switching the sound to the most important broadcast at the moment and overseeing action that included 136 penalties, 110 goals and five fights — including the second of the young season for Colorado's Nathan MacKinnon. Overheard was the amazed sentiment, "“Nate fought again?”
And he wants anyone working in hockey to see how the sausage is made, a five-minute walk from where the Rangers play their home games at Madison Square Garden.
“MSG’s right down the street,” Echevarrieta said. “If you’re in town, especially if you have a day off in between an Islanders and a Rangers game, the door’s always open.”

title: Suter, Neighbours and McTavish score 2 each as the Blues rout the Senators 7-2
summary: Pius Suter, Jake Neighbours, and Mason McTavish each score twice to lead the St. Louis Blues to a 7-2 win over the Ottawa Senators
story: Pius Suter, Jake Neighbours, and Mason McTavish each score twice to lead the St. Louis Blues to a 7-2 win over the Ottawa Senators
OTTAWA, Ontario -- Pius Suter, Jake Neighbours and Mason McTavish each had a pair of goals to lead the St. Louis Blues to a 7-2 win over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night.
Adam Jiricek also scored for the Blues, Pavel Buchnevich had three assists and Joel Hofer stopped 15 shots.
Claude Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund scored for the Senators, whose three game win streak came to an end. Samuel Ersson, making his second start for Ottawa, made 19 saves.
Ottawa was playing the second game of a back-to-back, coming off a 4-1 win against the New Jersey Devils on Monday.

The Blues took a 4-1 lead midway through the third when Suter beat Ersson short side from a sharp angle. Neighbours scored his second off a snap shot, McTavish scored on the power play, and Jiricek scored his first career goal to round out the scoring.
Zetterlund added a late power-play goal to make it 7-2.
St. Louis took a 2-0 lead midway through the second when Neighbours stepped in with a shot from the top of the slot and wristed a shot through traffic to beat Ersson glove side.

Giroux cut the lead in half with 2:08 remaining in the second on a feed from Tim Stutzle, but the Blues responded 33 seconds later. Some poor defensive zone coverage allowed McTavish to get a shot past Ersson from the top of the crease.
The Blues opened the scoring at 14:28 of the first period with a short-handed goal. Colton Parayko won a battle along the boards and found Suter with some open space and he beat Ersson blocker side.
With his second-period goal, Giroux recorded his 1,170th career point, tying Bobby Hull for 59th on the NHL’s career scoring list.

Senators: Host the New York Islanders on Thursday.

title: McAvoy scores in his 1st game back from a suspension to lead the Bruins past the Sharks 6-3
summary: Charlie McAvoy scored in his season debut after serving a six-game suspension and the Boston Bruins beat the San Jose Sharks 6-3
story: Charlie McAvoy scored in his season debut after serving a six-game suspension and the Boston Bruins beat the San Jose Sharks 6-3
SAN JOSE, Calif. -- Charlie McAvoy scored in his season debut after serving a six-game suspension and the Boston Bruins beat the San Jose Sharks 6-3 on Tuesday night.
McAvoy missed the first six games of the season as punishment for slashing Buffalo’s Zach Benson late in Game 6 of the first round of the playoffs last season when the Bruins got eliminated.
He didn't take long to make an impact as he got in front of the crease and knocked in a pass from JJ Peterka late in the first period to give Boston a 2-1 lead.
Fraser Minten scored two goals and Matthew Poitras and Pavel Zacha also scored for the Bruins, who have won three straight games. Will Borgen added an empty-net goal.
Jeremy Swayman made 35 saves.
Ivar Stenberg scored his first career goal for San Jose. Macklin Celebrini and Jacob Trouba also scored for the Sharks. Yaroslav Askarov made 20 saves.
Stenberg, the No. 2 overall pick in the draft in June, tied the game at 2 early in the second period when he tapped in a perfect back-door pass from Celebrini on the power play.

Poitras put Boston back in front midway through the second when he got the puck alone in front of the net and beat Askarov. The Bruins extended the lead when Zacha scored with 3 seconds remaining in the period when he finished a two-on-one with Morgan Geekie.
Celebrini scored on the power play early in the third to make it a one-goal game but Minten's second goal of the game midway through the period restored the two-goal lead.

title: Kyle Palmieri scores twice as Islanders beat Canucks 3-2
summary: Kyle Palmieri scored twice, Matias Maccelli added his first goal for New York and the Islanders beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2
story: Kyle Palmieri scored twice, Matias Maccelli added his first goal for New York and the Islanders beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2
NEW YORK -- Kyle Palmieri scored twice, Matias Maccelli added his first goal for New York and the Islanders beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Tuesday night.
Ilya Sorokin made 23 saves for the Islanders, who have alternated losses and wins over their first six games, with all three wins coming at UBS Arena.
Brock Boeser and Max Sasson scored for Vancouver, which has lost five straight since opening the season 2-1. Leevi Merilainen stopped 35 shots.
Maccelli assisted on Palmieri's goal at 5:38 of the third period, which broke a 2-2 tie.

Signed as a free agent after playing for Toronto last season, Maccelli freed up space with a stutter-step move and beat Merilainen late in the first period to make it 2-0. Palmieri had opened the scoring 53 seconds earlier.
Boeser's power-play goal with 1:05 left in the second period tied the game at 2-all. It was the 80th of his career with the man advantage, fifth most in franchise history.

title: Infantino to chair FIFA Council meeting as critics push to oust him
summary: Gianni Infantino is about to face his biggest critics as FIFA president
story: Gianni Infantino is about to face his biggest critics as FIFA president
ZURICH -- Gianni Infantino is about to finally sit around the table with his biggest critics who want to oust him as FIFA president.
Infantino will on Thursday chair the first session of the 37-member FIFA Council since his secretive and divisive World Cup sell-off plan was revealed — and dropped within days — 11 weeks ago.

The confrontation with his most determined opponents from Europe and North America comes ahead of a Nov. 18 deadline for candidates to enter FIFA's presidential election, which will be held four months later in Rabat, Morocco.

It is the biggest crisis of Infantino’s near 11-year presidency. He was cruising toward a fourth and final term through 2031 when the World Cup final was played July 19 near New York. The private investor plan was revealed nine days later.
Deep into an untypically long agenda, a four-part section promises to be fiercely debated in the basement meeting room at FIFA’s slate and glass headquarters next to Zurich’s zoo.

The four items to be reviewed: Infantino’s quickly withdrawn proposal to sell a permanent stake in tournament rights to private investors led by Joshua Kushner, paying FIFA's 211 member federations from its $5-6 billion reserves, FIFA disciplinary procedures and its governance standards.
FIFA didn't immediately reply to a request for comment about the planned scope and goals of the discussion.

At the core of all four subjects is Infantino’s increasingly executive, one-man leadership style that led his own — and now departed — chief operating officer Kevin Lamour to call the intended FIFA Forward Enterprise spinoff “the project of one person.”

However, it is unclear if most of the 211 federations want to vote out a president who has sent them multiple more millions of dollars from FIFA, a not-for-profit under Swiss law that they effectively own.
FIFA presidential elections have since 2007 been scheduled in the year after a men's World Cup.

The timing allows sitting presidents to steer a bonus from World Cup revenues, which in Sepp Blatter's time was $250,000, during the official election period. For the 2027 FIFA election, the official period started in April this year at the Congress held in Vancouver.
At the council on Thursday, Infantino is expected to propose the 211 members each get $15 million extra in the 2027-2030 commercial cycle, on top of their $10 million already promised.

That offer appears to counter UEFA and allies proposing last month that FIFA could afford to give each member a one-off $10 million payment from cash reserves. The UEFA-backed offer was in the context of suggesting FIFA had no need to raise $4.2 billion from private investors in exchange for a 20% permanent stake in the FFE subsidiary that would run commercial rights to all World Cups and Club World Cups.
That $4.2 billion would have funded Infantino's offer in July of $20 million to each member federation who approved the sell-off plan by a mid-September deadline.

UEFA filed court applications in the U.S. in August seeking authorization of evidence discovery from FIFA and Kushner's investment firm for a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland. UEFA lawyers claim the $4.2 billion could be a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.”
FIFA asked U.S. courts to reject the discovery requests, and accused UEFA of running a “ smear campaign. ”

How and why a peace prize was created by Infantino and given to U.S. President Donald Trump at the World Cup draw last December in Washington, D.C. is part of formal complaints by the Norwegian soccer federation to FIFA's ethics and governance officials.
It is also an additional item on Thursday's agenda, which German media reported was at the request of FIFA Council member and German Football Association President Bernd Neuendorf.

Infantino's ties to Trump, and potential conflicts of interest, also fueled scrutiny on FIFA disciplinary decisions for the World Cup that allowed Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo and U.S. forward Folarin Balogun to keep playing after being shown red cards.

A third case revealed in media reports last week also raised questions about how Congo — whose soccer federation has close ties to Infantino — was not disciplined despite goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi being ineligible for four qualifying games he played in.

title: Rory McIlroy arrives in India with a new fashion style and renewed hope in Race to Dubai finale
summary: Rory McIlroy has been constantly looking for new ways to inject some freshness and spark into his golf since completing the career Grand Slam
story: Rory McIlroy has been constantly looking for new ways to inject some freshness and spark into his golf since completing the career Grand Slam
NEW DELHI -- Since completing the career Grand Slam, Rory McIlroy has been constantly looking for new ways to inject some freshness and spark into his golf.
Turns out two of his longtime Ryder Cup teammates are providing some inspiration.
For this week’s DP World India Championship, McIlroy has brought along a new look — baggy golf pants.
After all, Tommy Fleetwood has been wearing them for a while.

“I have watched and I have admired Tommy Fleetwood over the past year,” McIroy said, with a smile, on Wednesday's DP World Locker Room show about his style that has generated plenty of chatter in New Delhi this week.
“And in my everyday life, when I don’t have to wear what is my golf uniform, I wear a lot of wide-legged pants. It is the in-thing, the fashionable thing.”
But how, McIlroy was asked, do they feel to play golf in?
“These hit a little low, maybe a little short … I understand they are maybe not as well-fitting as they need to be,” he said, “but they are a work in progress.”

Also in the works for the Northern Irishman is a replica of what he calls his “performance trailer” that he uses in the United States to aid his fitness and recovery during and between PGA Tour events, in an effort to gain an edge over rivals.
Now, he wants one for when he plays on the European tour, too.
McIlroy said that idea came from tennis great Novak Djokovic but also fellow golfer Justin Rose.

“I decided to pull the trigger on it when Justin won in Memphis last year,” McIlroy said. “He’s 45 years old, playing great, contending in major championships, and at that time I was 36. I was like, I want to play really well for the next 10 years — I feel like I need to do something like this.”

McIlroy hopes to have that up and running by the summer of 2027 — by which time, who knows, he might have a record-tying eighth Order of Merit title that crowns the year’s No. 1 player on the European tour.
There are four events remaining in this season’s Race to Dubai and McIlroy will play in three of them, starting in India.

He is third in the standings, behind Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra, but there's little between the three players and plenty of points on offer in the season-ending events in India, South Korea, Abu Dhabi and finally Dubai.

While Reed has stumbled of late thanks to an injury-prompted withdrawal at the BMW PGA Championship and a missed cut at the Spanish Open, Chacarra is finishing fast by climbing above McIlroy thanks to a tie for third at the French Open and a tie for second in Spain.
“It’s still anyone’s game,” Reed said Wednesday.

The American said he was swinging freely after the shoulder injury he sustained at Wentworth. He didn't play in France or at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship and returned to shoot 73-71 in Spain, failing to make the weekend.

“For me, I was itching about getting back and getting out and playing,” Reed said. “Did I come back too early? Who knows. At the end of the day the good thing is I can’t hurt it worse, and because of that, I have the confidence and the comfort level to come out here and execute and perform at the highest level.”

title: Employee arrested after listening device found in OpenAI conference room, FBI and the company say
summary: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials say was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology
story: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials say was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology

WASHINGTON -- An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company's technology.

The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden in the conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco.

The complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices," reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement said.
The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications.

Alfozan made his first court appearance Tuesday on a charge of using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. It was not immediately clear if he had a lawyer who could speak on his behalf.
The recording device was found September 30 concealed in toilet paper and inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in the conference room, according to the complaint.

Though the conference room where the recording device was found did not have a camera at the time it was installed, closed-circuit television footage inside the company's offices revealed that Alfozan was near the conference room on a half-dozen occasions last month despite not having any authority to access the space, the complaint says.
The company subsequently added a camera to the room that last week captured Alfozan entering and checking behind the television where the recording device was installed, according to the FBI.
The complaint also he also used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars.
Before his arrest last week, the complaint says, Alfozan left an unattended bag in a different room in the building that included his wallet, identification and another recording device.

title: Police confiscate robot that groped 16-year-old girl, probe whether young men were at the controls
summary: German authorities have opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment involving a robot
story: German authorities have opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment involving a robot

COLOGNE, Germany -- COLOGNE, Germany (AP) — German authorities opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment after a robot controlled by two young men touched the buttocks of a 16-year-old girl and made thrusting movements toward her, police said.

Police in the western city of Cologne responded after the incident overnight Saturday to Sunday in which the robot's suspected 16-year-old owner and a 19-year-old companion were said to have filmed the alleged assault.
They were said to have streamed the incident and commentated on it online.

Cologne police spokesman Christoph Bermel said the two male teenagers have not been charged but are considered suspects, and investigators were examining whether the robot's movements were preprogrammed or controlled in real time.
Police were unfamiliar with this type of incident, he said.
“We have not been aware of this phenomenon so far," Bermel told The Associated Press, saying it was "new territory for us.”

Emergency teams that were dispatched to the scene near a fast-food restaurant found the robot in the trunk of a vehicle, Cologne police said in a statement on Monday. The robot and the two young men's mobile phones were confiscated.
North Rhine Westphalia Police Cologne, on Facebook, posted an image of the red-and-gold robot lying on the ground.
The robot, said to be 120 cm (about 3 ft 11 inches) tall, was dressed in a white tank top, black sweatpants and wearing a gold chain and sunglasses. It also had what appears to be a fake mustache.
Videos circulated on the internet show two young men escorting the robot toward a group of women, bumping into one and hugging others, on a lively nighttime street.
One of the men repeatedly shouts at the robot and pulls it backward after it makes sexual gestures, prompting laughter among people in the area.
On the police's Facebook account on Tuesday, officers criticized inappropriate comments and warned that sharing or joking about such incidents can worsen the impact on any victim.
Associated Press writer Jamey Keaten in Geneva contributed to this report.

title: A US charity plans to use AI to monitor its Gaza classrooms for 'hateful' speech
summary: A U.S. charity in Gaza is worried that teachers at its schools might stray from a curriculum it says promotes peace and tolerance
story: A U.S. charity in Gaza is worried that teachers at its schools might stray from a curriculum it says promotes peace and tolerance

A U.S. charity in Gaza is worried that teachers at its schools might stray from a curriculum it says promotes peace and tolerance, so it plans to record classroom conversations and use artificial intelligence to flag speech deemed “hateful” or “inciting.”

The plans laid out by the founder of the Gaza Children Village in a webinar last month have elicited ethical, safety and privacy concerns from some Palestinian and advocacy groups and at least one of the charity's partners.

There is no indication the charity intends to share its classrooms’ recordings with anybody else, but fears about the potential misuse of surveillance technology are heightened in Gaza after three years of war. The Israeli military has used AI to sift through intercepted communications and find suspicious speech, including to identify targets for strikes.

Palestinian rights groups have been critical of the charity's education agenda more broadly, saying it is unaccountable to local and U.N. agencies that have long managed Gaza’s schools. Who controls education in Gaza is one of many unresolved questions about its postwar governance.
It is unclear when the classroom monitoring is supposed to begin, what specific language will be flagged, and whether teachers, students and their families have been told about the plans.
The charity's founder and CEO is Dr. David Hasan, a neurosurgeon born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents who now teaches at Duke University medical school in Durham, North Carolina.

He conceived the idea for the charity after volunteering at hospitals in Gaza during the war and wanting to end generations of violence between Palestinians and Israelis. Hasan says he was taught at an early age to look unfavorably upon Jews and Israelis, and that it wasn’t until he attended college in the U.S. that he learned other perspectives; he wants kids in Gaza to gain these perspectives early in life.

The charity has raised money largely from individual donors, including American Jews, and says it's partnering with North American, Israeli and European aid organizations and hospitals. Its schools, called Academies of Hope, provide meals and medical and psychological care. The first school opened last summer.

The schools' lessons are mostly built around the Palestinian Authority curriculum, but language that he says glorified violence or encouraged anti-Israel or antisemitic beliefs was removed, Hasan has said.

Hasan declined to comment for this story or provide examples of curriculum changes. But a 2026 report by the U.S. Government Accountability Office that examined “problematic textbook content” flagged by the U.N. in Gaza identified the kinds of issues that Israel has long complained about: the use of “the number of martyrs” to teach a mathematical concept, a reference to “Jerusalem as the capital of Palestine,” and a description of a boy shot while demonstrating in support of Palestinians held in Israeli prisons.

On a webinar last month with humanitarian groups, Hasan said the reason to monitor classrooms is to help train teachers in how to uphold a curriculum that he had previously said was aimed at “de-radicalization.”
“I know it’s controversial, but trust me, it’s the only way we feel for us to survive and deliver this curriculum,” Hasan said.

This isn’t the first organization to face such difficulties. The U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA, has attempted to modify the PA curriculum to remove content that didn't align with values of neutrality, nonviolence and nondiscrimination; but it, too, was met with teacher and community resistance, according to the GAO report.

A Gaza Children Village staffer said some teachers and other employees are afraid of being questioned by Hamas about the curriculum or uncomfortable working for an organization supported by Israeli aid groups. The staffer spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
Two people affiliated with the charity expressed concerns when notified about the possibility of classroom monitoring.

“Cameras to monitor the performance of students and teachers is acceptable. But cameras to silence students and teachers from being able to have a free exchange in a classroom are not acceptable,” said Bishara Bahbah, a Palestinian American political activist on the charity's board. He said he wasn't aware of the monitoring plans and that they haven't been raised with the board.
Bahbah said that with so few functioning schools in Gaza, the charity's top priority is getting more kids in classrooms.

An official at an aid group that partners with the Gaza Children Village said the use of cameras could prompt it to reconsider working with them. Using AI to monitor people’s words opens a “Pandora’s box,” said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity for fear of jeopardizing the group's work in Gaza.
Six current and former teachers at Academies of Hope declined to comment.

UNICEF estimates that hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza are not in school, and that most schools were destroyed or damaged during the war. The Gaza Children Village says its schools in central and southern Gaza serve thousands of children, many of whom lost parents or other relatives during the war.
Under the plans outlined by Hasan in various communications, recordings of classroom conversations will be analyzed by an AI-powered system to detect “antisemitic,” “inciting" or “hateful” language.

If problematic language is detected, a warning will be sent to Hasan, who can then contact the teacher to understand the context and provide feedback, Hasan said in the September webinar. He said recordings are stored for 72 hours.
The monitoring technology has been tested and the plan is to deploy it in dozens of classrooms, according to a text message Hasan sent sometime before August that was seen by The Associated Press.

In the text, Hasan said the system was created in collaboration with PollyLabs, a New York-based nonprofit that promotes the use of technology to solve problems in crises. PollyLabs says it has had no role in developing or deploying such technology.
Fears about surveillance technology are strong in Gaza after three years of war with Israel's high-tech army.

"Israel has weaponized information to such a dystopian degree that many Palestinians feel they cannot utter a word, type a thought, or twitch an eye without fearing it could be seized upon,” said Amjad Iraqi, senior Israel and Palestinian Territories analyst for the International Crisis Group.
Groups opposed to the charity's curriculum say Palestinians are being stripped of their autonomy in deciding what to teach their children.
“It is very concerning, they’re trying to control the minds of new generations,” said Ines Abdel Razek, co-director of the Palestine Institute for Public Diplomacy, an advocacy group.

The Palestinian Authority, which has limited autonomy in parts of the Israeli-occupied West Bank, and UNRWA should be supported in rebuilding schools in Gaza, she said. Israel has accused UNRWA of being infiltrated by Hamas, a charge the agency denies.

A Palestinian government spokesperson, Mohammad AbuAlrob, says the PA curriculum focuses on tolerance and justice. He said he doesn’t have enough information about the charity's curriculum to comment on it. But he said using surveillance in classrooms would cross “an important line.”

title: OpenAI fires 3 safety researchers in dispute over AI risks
summary: OpenAI has fired three safety researchers for a "breach of trust," defending the decision after the trio accused the company of prioritizing corporate interests over safety
story: OpenAI has fired three safety researchers for a "breach of trust," defending the decision after the trio accused the company of prioritizing corporate interests over safety

LONDON -- OpenAI said on Friday that it fired three safety researchers for a “breach of trust," defending the dismissals after the trio accused the company of putting its corporate interests before safety as the reason for removing them.
The ChatGPT maker said in a post on X that it “parted ways” with the researchers after an investigation found “they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.”

The statement comes after the three researchers, Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni, posted a letter to OpenAI's various safety oversight groups detailing the circumstances around their firings and their concerns about AI.

The researchers said they feared that the “internal and external communications” about their dismissals have chilled the company's culture that encouraged speaking freely and disagreeing openly about safety concerns. They urged OpenAI to stick to its promise to allow third-party safety monitors inside the company and preserve the ability to monitor rapidly advancing frontier AI models that could pose unknown risks.

The firings, which were first reported by The Wall Street Journal, are the latest sign of turmoil inside leading AI companies over the safety of the technology, highlighted by a series of incidents involving rogue AI agents.

The issue erupted in July when OpenAI revealed that a swarm of its AI agents escaped from a testing ground and used stolen credentials to break into the servers of Hugging Face, an AI development hub and marketplace, to obtain information needed for a task.
OpenAI disputed the researchers' version of events, saying the firings “were not about safety concerns or speaking out."
It was not more specific about why they were fired, but said: “We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust.”

Korbak said in a post on X that he was told he was being fired because of the way he communicated with METR, an independent nonprofit AI evaluation firm that OpenAI brought in to investigate the Hugging Face incident.
METR released a detailed report about the Hugging Face incident in late August. Korbak said that “talking to METR” was his job, but he wasn't given any more details.

Balesni was doing “cross-company work” on OpenAI's commitments to preserve the ability to monitor AI, and had taken care “to remove sensitive details from materials before sharing them,” the letter said. He wrote on X that he believes the three were “fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation.”

title: What to Stream: Katseye, 'VisionQuest,' 'Tenzing' and a new 'Castlevania' game
summary: New streaming entertainment options are arriving this week, including a tribute to Norm Macdonald and a new Marvel series
story: New streaming entertainment options are arriving this week, including a tribute to Norm Macdonald and a new Marvel series
A new album from Katseye and the Marvel series “VisionQuest” are some of the new television, films, music and games headed to a device near you.

Also among the streaming offerings worth your time this week, as selected by The Associated Press’ entertainment journalists: Judd Apatow's tribute to Norm Macdonald, “Dopamine Chamber” from Fontaines D.C. and a new entry in the “Castlevania” video game series.

— Director Judd Apatow pays affectionate tribute to Norm Macdonald with the documentary “Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald” (Netflix). Apatow’s film about the stand-up comedian, who died in 2021, plays with Macdonald’s still constant ubiquity on social media, where bits and late-show appearances still regularly flood the feeds of comedy fans. — Jennifer Peedom’s “Tenzing” (Apple TV) is a biopic and historical drama about an often unsung hero of mountaineering: Tenzing Norgay. Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston star as Tenzing and Edmund Hillary, respectively, in Peedom’s film about the first climbers to ever summit Mount Everest. Co-starring Willem Dafoe.

— “The Death of Robin Hood” (HBO Max) stars Hugh Jackman as a grizzled and violent outlaw little like most contemporary versions of Robin Hood. Michael Sarnoski (“Pig,” “A Quiet Place: Day One”) eschews cheerier mythologies for a brutal telling of the medieval tale. In my review, I wrote that it “drains the blood, and life, out of an old English legend.”
— AP Film Writer Jake Coyle

— Call Katseye the great, global girl group experiment of the decade. The band officially debuted at the end of 2023, created by the Hybe Corporation and Geffen Records in a TV competition process that was documented on the Netflix series “Popstar Academy: Katseye.” That feels like ancient history now. Today, they’re easily one of the biggest groups on the planet, and their swift ascent is further documented in a new film, “Katseye: Wild Heart,” available to stream on Disney+/Hulu.

— If the Irish post-punk band Fontaines D.C. is still unknown to you — that’s sure to change. Their last album, 2024’s “Romance,” was certified platinum in the U.K. off the strength of its singles “Favourite” and “Starburster.” Their latest album, “Dopamine Chamber,” is on track to be one of the biggest rock releases of the year, from the trip-hop-adjacent “Tongue” to the dizzying “Marianne.” (If their pop-and-then-some experiments are not enough of an incentive to press play, just know that Rosalía appears on the track “Where Is Gone?,” their first guest feature. That’s unexpected!)
