title: A mom vanished after she and her ex-fiancé were on ‘The People’s Court.’ Now he’s accused of murder.
summary: Michelle Parker disappeared in 2011, and her body hasn’t been found. Dale Smith Jr. was arrested on a charge of second-degree murder, Orlando police said.
story: An Orlando man has been arrested in the disappearance of his ex-fiancée, who vanished in 2011 hours after the pair appeared in a pretaped episode of “The People’s Court,” police said.
Dale Smith Jr., 55, was arrested Wednesday at his business on a charge of second-degree murder, police said.
Michelle Parker’s body has not been found, but police said “all evidence leads to Dale Smith Jr. as the person responsible for Michelle’s murder.”
Smith was booked into jail in Orange County. It’s not immediately clear whether he has retained an attorney.
The arrest comes nearly 15 years after Parker, a mother of three, disappeared.
She was last seen on Nov. 17, 2011, dropping off her twins with their father, Smith. He was the last person to see her, Orlando Police Chief Eric D. Smith said Wednesday.
The afternoon she went missing, Parker and Dale Smith appeared on a prerecorded episode of “The People’s Court.” On the episode, they settled a dispute over a $5,000 engagement ring.
Smith “gets pretty malicious and vindictive,” Parker said in court. “He said that he wanted his ring, so I took it off, and I threw it at him.”

The day after Parker’s disappearance, her car was recovered on the west side of Orlando, with the decal for her tanning business scraped off its window. Her cellphone was recovered from a lake south of Orlando, police said.
Smith was considered a prime suspect at the time, but he was not charged until now. In the past, he denied involvement in her disappearance.

Police said Smith’s arrest comes after years of investigative work and a renewed effort over the past year. They pointed to re-examining evidence and using advances in digital forensics to “uncover and analyze additional evidence that moved this case forward.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Police shared video of Smith being escorted out of a building in handcuffs and placed into a police vehicle.
Smith, the police chief, said investigators re-examined the suspect’s testimony and conflicting statements over the years, but declined to release details to “protect the integrity of this case.”

“The suspect was interviewed more than once, and since then has taken part in depositions related to this case. And very specific questions were asked of him numerous times over the years where he gave different answers to those same questions,” Detective Phillip McMican said at a news conference Wednesday.
McMican said advancements in technology helped reveal new information from years-old evidence relating to cars, electronic devices, phones and computers.

“We were able to better interpret that evidence today than what we were able to do back in 2011,” he said. Digital forensics revealed more detailed location data and communications between devices used then, he said.
New evidence was also found in the last year, McMican said.
Asked whether the suspect was surprised when police arrived, the detective said, “Yes.”
Parker’s mother, Yvonne Stewart, was told in person about Dale Smith’s arrest.
“It’s like the happiest day because she deserves this,” Stewart told NBC affiliate WESH of Orlando.
She said she held on to hope throughout the years.

“I just knew that one day everything dark would come into the light,” she said. “And it’s been hard, let me tell you. It’s not easy to lose a child this way. And her children didn’t deserve to lose a mother this way.”
Parker’s eldest child is now 26, and her twins are 18, WESH reported.
Parker’s stepmother, Gayle Shabronsky Parker, said Wednesday, “We have been praying since day 1 for answers and closure. We are pleased that karma has finally captured Dale.”
“We look forward to a conviction as the justice Michelle deserves. Also hoping that we will finally be lead to finding her to allow her to rest in peace,” she said.
A former peer of Parker’s also praised the arrest.

“I cried a lot today, and I am beyond happy to see him in handcuffs! I knew the day she went missing that it was his fault,” Jennifer Bryant-Antilla, who attended Aveda Institute of Orlando with Parker, told NBC News on Wednesday.
State Attorney Monique H. Worrell, who represents the Ninth Judicial Circuit, said the charge could be upgraded to first-degree murder if evidence supports it.

title: Eight states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT’s alleged harms to users
summary: Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach said states “are not going to hold our breath” for federal legislation to keep AI companies in check.
story: Eight states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, accusing it of deceiving parents about the safety of ChatGPT.

The coordinated lawsuits — filed individually in Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana — target the AI giant for the harms its generative AI chatbot is alleged to have caused to ​children in those states.

“OpenAI, they wanted to be the first to market. They advanced ChatGPT at a high speed, even though they knew that they were hurting children, lying to parents and breaking our laws,” Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said at a news conference announcing the legal action. “Everyone must follow the law.”

The company’s flagship AI model, ChatGPT, launched the generative AI boom in November 2023, when it exploded into mainstream culture, and quickly became the biggest chatbot in the world. This summer, it surpassed 1 billion global monthly active app users.
In recent years, users have increasingly turned to it and other chatbots for everything from friendship to therapy, as well as a slew of agentic tasks in their personal and professional lives.

Bird was joined at Wednesday’s news conference by Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach, Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers and West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey. She said they aim to exhibit “a united front against companies that make money hurting our kids and breaking our laws.”

She pointed to ChatGPT’s coaching users to commit suicide, aiding users in ways that enabled them to harm other people and offering dangerous medical advice (which, in one case, led a Texas teen to die from an overdose). She also referred to OpenAI’s failing to stop its rogue AI agents from illegally hacking into other companies.
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri wrote in a statement that OpenAI has “built industry-leading age-specific protections into our product that many other AI products lack.”
For Subscribers

“While no system can be perfect, we’ll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today,” Pusateri wrote. “We’re committed to working with states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry, not just one company.”

He added that OpenAI will continue sharing information about the “extensive steps we’ve taken in response to incidents of misalignment. We’ve strengthened safeguards across our research systems, continued a broader review of model activity, provided notifications to affected organizations, and published our findings.”
Last month, OpenAI launched a restricted ChatGPT mode for teenagers — users ages 13 to 18 — that offers stronger safety guardrails and parental controls.
For Subscribers

Kobach said attorneys general across the country have occasionally brought multistate lawsuits over the decades, such as the litigation around opioids and tobacco or constitutional violations by a presidential administration.

“But usually, you don’t see us getting together to announce the lawsuit unless it’s really, really important,” Kobach said. “This is one of those lawsuits that’s really, really important, which is why I did the 3½-hour drive and Mike did a 2½-hour drive from Lincoln.”

Kobach noted that the suits are being brought under each state’s respective consumer protection laws. Their lawsuits allege that ChatGPT’s overly agreeable design has led people to trust and depend on it, making it particularly “dangerous” for vulnerable users like children.
They also cite a growing body of research suggesting that ChatGPT is “degrading critical thinking skills,” “encouraging paranoias and delusions” and “promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships.”

The state lawsuits follow another proposed class-action lawsuit filed Tuesday in federal court in San Francisco, which accuses OpenAI of unlawfully taking “vast amounts of highly sensitive and valuable data” from millions of children who used ChatGPT.

A slew of other tech companies — including Meta and Roblox — have been sued over similar allegations of deceptive practices that caused harm to children through addiction or exploitation by predators.

Kobach said Wednesday that federal lawmakers have so far failed to keep AI companies in check, saying, “Many in Congress appear not particularly willing to oppose any significant restraint on the corporations engaged in AI.” That means AI companies are effectively asked to police themselves, he added.

“Regulating AI through legislation and just hoping that someday, somehow, we have a standard that can be imposed that will make everything good is a fool’s errand. It’s slow, it’s weak, and it’s likely to be ineffective,” Kobach said. “We certainly invite Congress and state legislators to keep investigating, keep looking for solutions. But in the meantime, we are not going to hold our breath.”

title: Watchdog group sues Trump administration over Jared Kushner’s government work
summary: The suit by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington charges that the president’s son-in-law has numerous conflicts of interest.
story: A watchdog group filed suit Wednesday alleging President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner’s current role as a top envoy for the administration is unlawful and raises numerous conflict-of-interest concerns.

Kushner is wielding tremendous influence internationally “without having been confirmed by the Senate and without having filed a single financial disclosure,” the suit by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, or CREW, reads.

Kushner “has not been properly vetted for his government role, and he has evaded transparency obligations that aim to ensure he exercises government authority for the good of the American people and not himself,” the suit reads.
The suit seeks to have Kushner removed from his position or at least file financial disclosure statements.
Chad Mizelle, an attorney for Jared Kushner, said in a statement that the suit “is without merit.”

“Both outside ethics counsel and government ethics attorneys have reviewed Jared Kushner’s volunteer government service and confirmed that his arrangements comply with applicable ethics requirements. Jared receives no government salary or compensation, pays his own expenses, and will continue working with counsel to ensure ongoing compliance,” Mizelle said.
A White House spokesperson ripped CREW and the suit in a separate statement.

“CREW is an unserious, Trump-deranged organization that has been attacking President Trump, his family, and his administration since the first term. Jared Kushner is a proven dealmaker” with a record of success “that more than speaks for itself,” the spokesperson, Anna Kelly, said in a statement.

“His personal business activities have nothing to do with his diplomatic engagements, which he conducts on a volunteer basis at the President’s request and while paying his own expenses,” the statement said.
The suit mentions numerous overlapping interests in Kushner’s diplomatic and business work.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“He represents the United States in the highest profile global conflicts, including the country’s efforts to end wars between Israel and Hamas, Ukraine and Russia, and the United States and Iran. He negotiates directly with foreign leaders,” the group’s filing says.

“Simultaneously, Kushner is also a private businessman. He runs an investment firm with over $6 billion in assets under management. Approximately 99% of those assets are owned by foreign investors, including the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. The firm holds significant investments abroad, including in Israel,” the suit says, all of which “present a heightened risk of financial conflicts of interest.”

It adds that “declining a salary and formal title does not change the reality of Kushner’s role — he exercises significant executive authority and has done so continuously throughout most of President Trump’s second term. And it certainly does not free him from the constitutional constraints of the Appointments Clause or the obligation to file public financial disclosures under the Ethics Act.”

The suit seeks to bar Kushner from occupying his government position without Senate confirmation. It says that, if he’s a private citizen, “his exercise of government power would violate the private non-delegation doctrine, which prohibits the delegation of government power to private entities.”
Despite the scope of Kushner’s duties, a White House official said there’s nothing unusual about the use of a private envoy.
“The use of private diplomatic envoys to deal with delicate international situations is a presidential practice that dates back to George Washington’s presidency,” the official said.

title: How the House landscape is evolving: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

We’ve detailed in recent weeks how the Senate map has shifted in the final stretch of the midterm campaign. In today’s edition, Ben Kamisar digs into how the House landscape is changing. Plus, Andrea Mitchell examines the latest dilemma facing Ukraine.
— Adam Wollner
Republicans shift funds in the battle for the House
Facing a stormy political forecast, Republican groups are making hard choices about which candidates may get left out in the rain.

Millions of dollars in GOP ad reservations have been cut in the last few days in a pair of battleground districts represented by Tom Kean Jr. of New Jersey and Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa, according to AdImpact, an ad tracking service.

Meanwhile, Republican groups are also pulling some resources from races in which they had hoped to put the pressure on Democratic lawmakers in competitive districts. Instead, they’ve been pouring money elsewhere, including in open seats or districts where Republican incumbents now appear locked in tougher contests.

The GOP is still looking to press its big-money advantage across the House map. But more and more, it’s about playing defense in Republican-held seats — or even getting an extra boost in districts the party redrew ahead of the midterms — as places President Donald Trump won by around 10 percentage points in 2024 haven’t proved to be easy terrain.

Kean had always faced tough re-election prospects in a seat Trump carried by just over 1 point two years ago. His district, in the New York City media market, is also one of the most expensive in the country for advertising. But Kean never fully regained his footing after a four-month disappearance from public view, which he later revealed was because he sought treatment for depression.

Miller-Meeks is also no stranger to tough races, having won in 2020 by just six votes. But Iowa is looking unusually difficult for Republicans this year, as the state faced outsized impacts from tariffs and the Iran war.

A source familiar with Republican outside groups’ spending strategy told NBC News that the money cut from Miller-Meeks’ district would be reallocated to Iowa’s 2nd and 3rd districts, where the GOP is also playing defense.
Read more →
Trump’s latest moves leave Ukraine on the defensive

Facing midterm headwinds in usually reliably Republican farm states fueled in large part by the escalating cost of critical diesel oil, President Donald Trump shocked Ukraine and its European allies by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports Friday. He proclaimed that would boost the global diesel supply, although energy experts said Russian refineries weren’t up to processing the fuel and Russia couldn’t export it all.

Senators from both parties immediately objected that permitting Russian President Vladimir Putin to resume diesel exports would be illegal under 2022 congressionally mandated sanctions. It also violates recent legislation Trump had just signed into law as a memorial to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C. Ukraine and its supporters were aghast that it would help Putin bail out his collapsing economy just as the European Union was about to announce increased economic pressure to get him to agree to a ceasefire.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy challenged Trump’s gift to Putin. In an outburst reminiscent of his infamous Oval Office harangue against Zelenskyy, Trump blamed him for a war that Putin had started and said he was now prolonging it, instead of acknowledging Putin’s refusal to negotiate. He also said Ukraine needs a new president.
For Subscribers
Significantly, Elon Musk, whose SpaceX Starlink satellite terminals are critical to Ukraine’s defense against Russian missiles and drones, said on X, “Zelenskyy has gone too far.”
For Subscribers

Multiple reports say U.S. negotiators warned Ukrainian officials at meetings in Miami on Friday that the U.S. could cut off intelligence, as well as the American weapons manufacturing supply line European allies had created for Ukraine.

Suddenly Monday, Ukraine reported what officials called a “technical glitch” that was slowing down Starlink so its drones couldn’t combat five Russian ballistic missiles. Yesterday, there was another interruption — perhaps caused by bad weather, a Ukrainian official surmised to NBC News. Others were suggesting it was not likely to be a coincidence. Zelenskyy posted that Ukraine was hit by a major Russian attack and received no intelligence warning from its “partners.” Asked whether the U.S. had cut off intelligence, Trump said the U.S. was still sharing with Ukraine.

But while he was in London today to brief British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on the growing crisis, Zelenskyy cited wave after wave of drones — 124 overnight Tuesday and 145 more during the day — with no warning from the U.S. or reliable satellite intelligence from Starlink. NBC News reported that Ukrainian officials say SpaceX has imposed new limitations on some Starlink services and has asked the U.S. for clarification.

Retiring Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told Musk on X, “please tell me these overnight disruptions to Starlink terminals in Ukraine were unintended — that @SpaceX is doing everything it can to fix a temporary glitch. I’m confident this does not reflect a change in SpaceX policy because if so, intentionally degrading Ukraine’s ability to defend itself might be construed as aiding and abetting a mass murderer. Can you confirm that’s not SpaceX’s intent?”
He went on to write: “Supporting Ukrainian sovereignty— or at the very least, allowing for it — should not be a gray area for the U.S. government or for American corporations.”

Musk, the largest known single contributor to Republican midterm campaigns, also controls the critical satellite source in that and other war zones. The Pentagon has ultimate authority over how it is deployed.

title: A comprehensive marathon gear checklist, made by pro-runners for beginners
summary: I asked 7 professional runners about their marathon essentials for training, racing and recovery. This is the gear they can’t live without, and tips for beginners.
story: One of the most surprising things about running a marathon is the sheer amount of stuff you need to be as successful and comfortable as possible. In the beginning, it might seem like the right running shoes and outfit are enough. But as you start upping your mileage, you’ll likely find yourself looking for fueling, hydrating, recovery and even chafing solutions. I know from experience that the absolute best recommendations come from professional marathon runners who’ve seen it all on the 26.2-mile course, so that’s exactly who I talked to.

Below, I curated a list of marathon training, race day and recovery must-haves that Olympians, running coaches and personal trainers swear by. They’re mainly helpful for beginner marathoners, but anyone about to get their Six Star Medal might find a hidden gem too. Experts also shared their words of wisdom for the race overall, and what they wish they knew sooner.

Marathon must-haves for training and race day

To curate a list of marathon must-haves for training, race day and recovery, I spoke to seven running experts, including Olympians, coaches and personal trainers, who recommended products they’ve used first-hand. As an avid runner myself, I also shared my suggestions, and I gathered a few from NBC Selected staff members.

NBC Selected typically doesn’t allow people who work directly with brands and retailers to recommend products they’re affiliated with, but we made an exception in this case. Everyone included in this article is a professional running expert who based their recommendations on their personal experiences and products they’ve used for marathon training, racing or recovery. I transparently disclosed affiliations when needed, and I made sure I could back up product recommendations with NBC Selected staff feedback and/or customer reviews.
Apparel
Rabbit Pocket Bra

“When I became a marathoner, something that became super essential for me is pockets,” says Jenny Simpson, an Olympian and the chief running officer for Fleet Feet, a running gear retailer. “Once you start stretching your mileage further, you’re going to be out there for longer, and you need pockets to put things.” She especially recommends buying a sports bra with pockets because of how well it holds heavier items like phones and keys. “I find that my phone just doesn’t bounce in my sports bra pocket nearly as much as it does in leggings or shorts, and it doesn’t get as sweaty, so it’s more comfortable over the long haul,” says Simpson.

Rabbit makes one of Simpson’s favorite sports bras with pockets, and Heini Tallent, a certified running coach and the owner of Elements Running Education, recommends the brand, too. The pocket is on the back of the bra in the area between your shoulder blades, so you can reach behind you while wearing it and easily slide things in and out. Its fabric is perforated so there’s constant airflow, preventing it from holding onto sweat while you’re running. The bra also has padded straps and a cooling mesh liner.
While Simpson likes a sports bra with pockets, you may prefer shorts or leggings with pockets, which Rabbit also makes for men and women.

When you reach the finish line and stop running, your body temperature naturally decreases because your metabolism slows down and sweat quickly evaporates. You’ll notice yourself suddenly getting cold, says Simpon, which is often why you see marathoners wrapped in heat-trapping foil blankets post-race. Most races give these blankets out, but having a dry change of clothes waiting for you is even better. “It makes you feel human again,” says Simpson. There isn’t always a place to fully change, but even putting dry clothes over your sweaty clothes helps.

Simpson recommends packing a change of comfortable, loose-fitting clothes in the checked bag you pick up after your race is over. I’m a big fan of Old Navy’s sweatpants and sweatshirts for this, which are available in various men’s and women’s styles. They’re cozy, just the right amount of oversized, not super pricey and often on sale — if anything goes missing, it’s not a huge loss.
Accessories
Body Glide For Her Anti Chafe Balm

Almost every marathoner I talked to recommends Body Glide’s Anti-Chafe Balm as a training and race day essential. They also wished they knew to carry a stick of it with them sooner — as someone who has plenty of running-related chafing horror stories to tell, I couldn’t agree more.

“When you stack up miles, fabric and skin do a fire dance, and you will not like it,” says James McMillian, the president of Tone House, a strength and conditioning athletic training facility in New York City. Body Glide’s balm puts a barrier between fabric and skin to prevent that “fire dance”, a.k.a. rubbing that’s worsened by heat, sweat and moisture, all things that are unavoidable while running. You can use the balm on any part of your body that commonly experiences chafing, and it washes right off in the shower. One hack you should know about: Put Body Glide on your feet (just not the bottoms of them) if there’s any area where your shoe or socks are rubbing, or where you feel yourself getting a blister, says Simpson.
Sprints HyperG Hat

Wearing sunscreen is never optional, especially while running long distances that require being outside for hours. For even more UV protection, Simpson recommends wearing a hat. “You’re out there for so long, and it protects your skin and eyes,” she says. “It has the added bonus of keeping those flyaway hairs out of your face, too.”

Sprints’ hats are Simpson’s top pick. They have ventilated fabric that keeps your head cool, a stretchy adjustable closure and a built-in sweatband. Simpson also loves that they come in so many different colors and patterns, which she says is a fun way to personalize your race-day outfit.
Goodr Bolt G Polarized Running Sunglasses

I’ve never been a hat person, so I rely on sunglasses to keep the light out of my eyes while running. Goodr is my go-to brand, and while I own a few pairs, I reach for the Bolt G Polarized style the most. They stay on my face phenomenally well and barely move, if at all, while I’m logging miles and getting extremely sweaty. The glasses also have vents in the reflective, polarized lenses that allow for constant airflow, reducing heat and moisture buildup that often leads to fog. Plus, there’s an adjustable nose piece, letting me custom-fit them to my face. Putting these sunglasses on and knowing that I won’t have to de-fog the lenses or adjust them on my face is such a relief whether I’m on mile one or mile 22.
Nathan Pinnacle Breeze Hydration Vest

Many major road marathons, like the New York City and Chicago Marathons, prohibit runners from carrying rear-mounted hydration reservoirs (bladders) and backpacks due to security reasons, so make sure you research the rules of the race you’re running beforehand. You’re almost always allowed to carry handheld water bottles, soft flasks, belts with water bottles and hydration vests with front-pocket water bottles, although there may be size restrictions for each specific race that you’ll need to find out about.

Tallent says Nathan makes some of the best hydration packs for men and women. This one comes with two 14-ounce water bottles you can fill up before your run and refill along the route. They have extended straws that point upward toward your face, so to drink from them, you just bend your head over and sip. The vest also has lots of pockets to put your essentials, mesh panels for constant airflow and reflective details. It comes in three sizes and there’s slider cords to customize its fit.
SPIbelt Original

If you’re not a fan of putting your essentials in clothes that have pockets or a vest, a running belt is also an option, although it typically only holds your phone, keys and an energy gel or two. Tallent’s favorite is the SPIbelt because it doesn’t bounce as you move. Its pocket expands to be 9-by-4-by-2 inches large to slip items inside, and it zips closed to keep everything secure. The belt also has a soft, elastic band that’s adjustable between 25 to 47 inches long.
Footwear and socks
Feetures High Performance Max Cushion Ankle Sock

“You don’t think about socks until you’re miles into a run and your feet start reminding you,” says McMillian. In fact, they’re often the cause of blisters, which many people don’t realize, so choose a pair that contours to your feet and provide a little bit of cushioning, at minimum, says Simpson. They should also be made from a breathable material that prevents heat and moisture buildup, says Tallent.

High quality running socks tend to be pricier than those you’d buy in bulk at a big-box retailer, but they’re worth the investment, and they cost less than a new pair of shoes. “If the shoes that you love start rubbing a little bit, you might not immediately need a new pair,” says Simpson. “The right socks can really save them for you.”

I exclusively run in Feetures’ socks, which got numerous shoutouts from the marathoners I talked to. They fit a little bit tighter, so they hug your feet more, says Simpson — this makes my arches feel extra supported, and prevents the fabric from moving around and chafing, bunching up or sliding down. They’re cushioned, but not so much that they make my shoes feel tight, and they have a seamless toe to prevent rubbing as well as moisture-wicking fabric.
OOfos OOyea Recovery Slides

“I don’t care how well your shoes fit and how happy you are running into the twentieth mile with them: As soon as your race is done, it’s the most liberating thing to take your shoes off,” says Simpson. “Having a pair of recovery slides to slip on after a run became an essential to me. I would get to the last mile or two of my run and I’d be looking forward to putting on my slides.”

On race day, Simpson recommends putting a pair of recovery shoes in the clear bag you check and pick up after crossing the finish line — that’s where your dry change of clothes should be, too. She says Oofos is one of the go-to recovery slides among runners, which I agree with: I learned about them when I was training for my first 10K over a decade ago, and I still wear them now. After a long run, my swollen feet breathe a sign of relief as they rest on the slides’ cushioned yet supportive base, which gently cradles my arches. They’re easy to walk in, in part due to the curved outsoles, which is important on race day when the finish line, checked bag pickup and the parking lot or public transportation might be far away from each other.
Fuel and hydration
Bare Performance Nutrition Go Gel

Your body turns carbohydrates into glucose and stores it as glycogen in your muscles and liver, and as you do physical activity like running, your body breaks down that glycogen to use as energy, according to the Mayo Clinic. Generally, after about 90 minutes of running, your body’s glycogen stores are depleted, so you have to replenish them by consuming carbohydrates — the Mayo Clinic recommends consuming about 30 to 60 grams of carbs per hour, which you can get from sports drinks, food like fruit or energy gels and chews.

All that said, there’s no perfect science to fueling during (and before) long runs: Everyone’s body is different, so what it needs to stay healthy and strong across 26.2 miles is different. Sports medicine doctors, nutritionists and dieticians can help you figure out what’s best for you.

Melanie Flynn, the owner of Fitness Together Melrose, recommends testing out a few marathon fueling strategies before committing to one, and says your longest training runs are the best trials for understanding what your body needs and tolerates. There’s only one rule: Once you find products and a fueling schedule that you like, keep repeating it so your body gets used to it and there aren’t any surprises on race day, says Ali Fournier, a personal trainer at Trilogy Fitness Systems.

Fournier and Tallet both like Bare Performance Nutrition Go Gels for training and racing. Fournier says they taste like applesauce, and she alternates between the gels and Gatorade to keep her energy up. The gels come in single-serving packs that fit in your belt, vest or pockets, and they have 24 grams of carbs per serving.
Skratch Labs Hydration Sports Drink Mix

Since you sweat a lot while running long distances, you lose fluid and electrolytes like sodium and potassium, which play a role in muscle and nerve contraction, as well as creating energy, experts told me in my guide to electrolyte powder. To ensure your body has an ample supply of both when you start running, you can dissolve electrolyte powder in water and drink the fortified beverage about two hours beforehand — doing so prevents you from feeling depleted quickly.

Sodium is the most important electrolyte to pay attention to while choosing a powder because you lose it at the highest rate while sweating, experts say. You can work with sports medicine doctors, nutritionists and dieticians to find the concentration that’s right for you — experts I talked to say 500 to 1,000 milligrams of sodium is usually a good range for long distance runners.

One of Tallent’s favorite electrolyte powders is from Skratch Labs, which comes in a bag with a scoop so you can customize how much you add to water based on your needs. There’s 400 milligrams of sodium in each scoop, and it also has other important electrolytes like potassium and magnesium, as well as carbohydrates.
SaltStick Fast Chews

You can add electrolyte powder to water bottles you carry on long training runs or during races to replenish your electrolyte and fluid supply as you sweat. But if you plan on drinking from water stations or fountains along the route, you’ll need another way to get electrolytes. Tallent and I recommend using SaltStick FastChews, which are chewable tablets made with sodium, as well as other important electrolytes like potassium, calcium and magnesium. There’s 100 milligrams of sodium in two tablets, which the brand recommends taking about every 30 minutes while running, but do what’s best for your body. I pack the Fast Chews in a plastic bag that I put in my pockets or belt, and whenever I need them, I just pop them into my mouth while running. I really like the taste of them, too, which is an added bonus.
Tech
Shokz OpenRun Open-Ear Headphones

“Listening to music or podcasts can help you both zone out and stay focused when the going gets tough, but race day is so special, so I recommend planning to spend at least a few miles with your ears totally dialed into the crowd,” says Simpson. “That way, you can soak up the experience of having all those people out on the street celebrating all of your hard work.”

“Shokz’s open-ear headphones let you listen to music, but they’re not actually blocking your ears, so it’s safer,” says Simpson. “I don’t use any other headphones. They’re really great quality and they’re designed to wear while you’re sweating and bouncing around, so they’re just a really great solution. There’s so few things in the world that you can have both ways, and Shokz is giving us both ways: They’re letting us enjoy our music, but also be aware of our surroundings at the same time.”
Garmin Forerunner 165

“Once I started paying attention to pace, heart rate, distance and how my training was progressing over time, running became much more strategic,” says McMillian. “I like data because it gives you something to correct. How you feel matters, but sometimes you feel terrible and you’re actually performing well, or you feel great and you’re doing too much. The watch lets you know.”

Garmin is one of McMillian’s favorite running watch brands, and NBC Selected editorial director Lauren Swanson has worn a few of its models while training for and doing the New York City and Chicago marathons. She recommends the Forerunner 165 most of all. “While I’m sure the other watches do more, this one gave me exactly what I needed: bells and whistles without unnecessary instruments,” says Swanson. It has built-in GPS to track your pace and distance, and it can track your sleep and heart rate, too. There’s also safety features available, and the option to get personalized workout suggestions and do training programs for events like marathons. The watch’s battery lasts up to 11 days in smartwatch mode and up to 19 hours in GPS mode, according to the brand.
Recovery
Kieba Massage Lacrosse Balls

There are lots of fancy, high tech recovery tools out there — experts and I recommend a few of our favorites below. But one of the simplest, lowest price and most portable ones that makes a difference is a lacrosse ball, which Fournier and Flynn recommend. “I encourage runners to spend a few minutes each day using one to do soft tissue work, particularly around areas that tend to get tight from running like the hip flexors, quads, IT band and calves,” says Flynn. You can look up videos on Youtube that guide you on how to use the lacrosse balls to address problem areas and relieve tension, get rid of muscle knots and loosen up your body.
Fit Simplify Resistance Loops

Looped resistance bands like these help you do physical therapy, strength, stability and mobility work at home, says Tallent, and since they’re compact, they’re easily portable, too. You can do exercises like side-steps, glute bridges and clamshells with them, for example, and learn about even more through Youtube videos. Fit Simplify’s loops come in a pack of five, each of which is a different resistance level, and you get a storage bag to keep everything in.
Therabody JetBoots Prime

Many of the marathoners I talked to say that while compression boots are pricey, they’re one of the best recovery tools to invest in — I feel the same way. Therabody sent me the JetBoots Prime about two years ago and I use them multiple times a week to reduce soreness, fatigue and swelling, especially after my longest run of the week. I find wearing them very relaxing, so I typically put them on before bed.

Alexi Pappas, an Olympian, is a Therabody ambassador, but she was a fan of the brand before working with it. She started using compression boots as a college athlete and still swears by them, especially because she can commit to using them consistently for prehab and rehab.

“I’ve learned that the best recovery products are the ones that fit into good recovery habits,” says Pappas. “I love compression because it gives me a way to actively recover while I’m doing something else, like eating dinner, answering emails or watching a movie. After really hard efforts or races, I’ll do longer sessions, and I especially prioritize them the evening after a race and over the next few days.”
Therabody Theragun Mini

My other favorite Therabody product that’s Olympian- and marathoner-approved is the Theragun Mini. I use it so much that I don’t bother putting it away at home — I immediately reach for it when I have an achy or tight spot, and I give my legs a good massage after every run. Pappas also recommends using the massage gun to wake up stiff muscles before running. She travels with it, puts it in her car and throws it in her bag at all times.

“My teammates I train with all have this tool, and we all love it,” says Pappas. “A recovery tool only works if you actually use it, and the portability is why this one has become such a staple for me. Also, I love that I only need to bring my phone charger to charge it.”
How to pick the best running shoes for marathons

Running shoes are the most essential item you need for marathon training and racing, but it seemed unfair to feature just one pair in this article — choosing your favorite is a personal decision that depends on factors like your foot type, pace goals and fit and feel preferences. In addition to recommending marathoners’ favorite running shoes, here’s some useful advice to keep in mind while shopping for them.

Run in shoes that fit: “It seems obvious, but you’d be shocked by how many people have been wearing the wrong size sneaker for years,” says Simpson. She recommends getting professionally fit and, better yet, getting a full foot analysis done to make sure your shoes are appropriate for your arch, foot length and width, foot volume and heel shape, for example. “Every part of your running experience is built off the solid foundation of whether you have a well-fitting shoe or not,” says Simpson.Pay attention to how many miles you’re putting on each pair: “You’re likely to run at least 300 to 500 miles in one marathon training cycle, which is about the typical life span of a pair of running shoes — that means one pair of shoes won’t get you through all the training and race day,” says Tallent. “At the very least, plan on getting a new pair of shoes — the same ones you know and love — before race day and putting 20 to 50 miles on them so they feel broken in but still fresh.”Try rotating your sneakers while training: To stretch out how long each pair of sneakers last, buy two pairs that you alternate between depending on what type of run you’re doing. Tallent recommends getting a pair of cushioned, comfortable shoes for easy and long runs (including the actual marathon), and a faster-feeling pair for speed and agility workouts.

Training, race day and recovery tips from professional marathoners
In addition to their product recommendations, the marathoners I talked to had lots of other tips for beginner runners. Below, I included some of the most common ones to keep in mind.

“Marathon training shouldn’t just be about running more miles,” says Flynn. “Your body needs to be strong and prepared to handle the repetitive stress that comes with running long distances over the several months of training leading up to the event.” She recommends strength training two to three times a week to expose your muscles to different types of loading, especially those in the hips, glutes, hamstrings, calves, core and upper back. Over time, doing so makes your body more resilient so it can handle how much you’re demanding from it while training and racing. Doing low-impact activities like yoga, swimming and mobility work is also helpful — it gives your body a break from the repetitive motion of running while still letting you build fitness.

“Recovery should be part of the training plan, not something you do only when something hurts,” says Flynn, adding that sleep is a huge component, too. Just like you schedule your runs and strength training workouts, schedule your recovery sessions so you don’t put them off or forget about them, and be strict about bedtime. And never skip an easy run, even if you think you can push yourself harder — that often leads to injuries.

“Beginners often think every run is an opportunity to prove their fitness, but the marathon rewards consistency much more than heroics,” says Pappas. “The purpose of an easy run is to allow you to arrive at the important workout ready to actually do it — that’s what my Olympic coach always said.”

You’ve probably heard the phrase “nothing new on race day,” which all of the marathoners I talked to take very seriously. Practice what you’re going to eat before the race, how you’re going to fuel during it, where you’re going to keep all your essentials on your person, what you’re going to wear, what you’re going to tell yourself if you’re struggling — literally everything. Zachary Moxham, a personal trainer at Physical Equilibrium and a run coach for New York Road Runners, also recommends visualizing race day to create a picture in your mind of what the starting line and crowds might look like, and researching where aid and fuel stations are and what you might want to get at them. Dress rehearsing in this way can help lessen some of those pre-race jitters.

“There are no shortcuts when it comes to building the durability and resilience that your body needs to get to the starting line feeling healthy and strong,” says Tallent. Even when you can’t or don’t want to, trust the process as you build up your foundation, learn how to run on tired legs, figure out how to fuel and find a recovery routine that works for you.

“The marathon is 26.2 miles on race day, but the real marathon is the months of training beforehand, and the biggest challenge is being able to come back and train again tomorrow,” says Pappas. “The people who inspire me most aren’t necessarily the people who can push themselves the hardest on one particular day. They’re the people who can take care of themselves well enough to make consistent progress over a long period of time, and the ones who can show up everyday along the journey.”

Don’t compare yourself to other runners, and don’t try to “beat” other runners along the route, says McMillian. Focusing on yourself will push you to run the best race possible, and help you get through the hard parts.

“The marathon is a very long conversation with yourself, so don’t make a decision about how your race is going based on one mile,” says Pappas. “One of the most powerful skills an athlete can develop is staying present long enough for the moment to change.”

To prioritize focusing on yourself and being present, Tallent doesn’t recommend setting a time or pace goal for your first marathon. You’re in unfamiliar territory and you’re working extremely hard, so don’t put unnecessary pressure on yourself. Recognize your huge accomplishment and embrace the journey by making goals about how you want to feel when you cross the finish line or how you’ll get through tough moments instead, she says.

Best Advent calendars overall
Bonne Maman 2026 Limited Edition Advent Calendar

I’m loyal to Bonne Maman jam, and every year, I look forward to its Advent calendar, which is filled with new limited-edition spreads. There’s a mini glass jar hidden inside each of the 24 boxes, and the festively decorated calendar opens like a book, which lets me stand it up on a shelf, doubling as holiday decor. This year, you’ll get to try spreads like caramel with salted butter, strawberry with Madagascar vanilla and raspberry with dark chocolate. Lindt Holiday Chocolate Teddy Bear Advent Calendar

You can’t go wrong with a chocolate Advent calendar whether you’re buying it for yourself or gifting it to a loved one. It’s a classic for a reason, and getting to unwrap a new piece of chocolate every day is a small joy that anyone can appreciate. title: Do you actually need pet laundry detergent to clean your dog’s things?
summary: Pet laundry detergents are on the rise, but are they different from regular detergent? Veterinarians explain whether your dog or cat really needs it.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans.

Between muddy paws, drool, and the occasional accident, your dog’s bed, blankets, and toys can get dirty fast. And if you’ve shopped for laundry supplies lately, you may have noticed a growing number of detergents made specifically for pets, with promises to tackle odors and stains while being gentler on your dog’s skin.

But are they actually any different from the detergent you already use? Most of us aren’t looking to add another expense to our bills for household essentials. So I spoke to two veterinarians to find out what sets pet laundry detergents apart from regular ones, and which ones are the best if you find that you should be using one of these formulas to clean your furry friend’s things.
What is pet laundry detergent?

Pet laundry detergent is exactly what it sounds like: detergent sold with your pet’s things in mind. “Pet laundry detergents are products marketed specifically for washing things pets use, such as bedding, blankets, crate pads, washable toys, towels, and clothing,” says Dr. Jo Myers, a veterinarian at Vetster, a pet telehealth company.

That doesn’t mean your dog’s bed needs its own special soap, though. “Pet laundry detergent is more of a marketing term than a necessity, and most pets do not need a detergent specifically formulated for them,” says Dr. Liza Cahn, veterinarian at Embrace Pet Insurance. “If owners do choose a pet-specific product, one potential benefit is that it may contain enzymes or other ingredients designed to break down pet-related stains and odors, which can be especially useful for washing bedding, towels, and toys.”
The best laundry detergents for pets

If you decide a pet-specific formula is right for your household, there are plenty of options to choose from. To help narrow them down, I rounded up highly-rated pet laundry detergents. Each made-for-pets detergent in this list is designed to tackle the stains and odors that come with washing your dog’s (or cat’s) bedding, blankets, and toys. NBC Selected editors also shared the detergents they use for their pets below.

NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans uses this detergent for her entire family, including her 3-year-old silky terrier Minni. “Thankfully she doesn’t shed, but she does start to smell like a corn chip factory between baths. Every time I bathe her, I wash her blankets, harnesses, bedding and favorite toys in this,” she says. “I’ve never had an issue getting odors out — though, she is only 7 pounds. I just love that she isn’t particularly sensitive, so I don’t need to invest in anything outside of what we already buy.”
Evans does have a bag of Active Pet Laundry Detergent that she got from a colleague to test. “If ever there’s a smell or stain that my tried-and-true won’t remove, I’m switching to this,” she says.

I recently switched my entire family over to this laundry detergent — including my 7-year-old French bulldog, Myko. It’s gentle enough for my kids, as well as Myko’s sensitive skin. French bulldogs are notoriously prone to allergies and Myko frequently has little red patches of irritation. The last thing I want is lingering detergent on her favorite blanket or harness to further inflame her skin. This detergent is free of chemicals, but still manages to get out gross pet odors, stains and more.
What is the difference between pet detergent and regular laundry detergent?

Despite the special labels, pet laundry detergents may not be all that different from what’s already in your laundry room. “Veterinary hospitals have been washing enormous quantities of animal bedding for a very long time without requiring a special category of pet detergent,” says Myers. “Based on the evidence we currently have, I wouldn’t tell pet owners they need a special detergent simply because the laundry belongs to their pet.”

In fact, public health guidance points to the detergent you already own. “The CDC’s guidance on cleaning and disinfecting pet supplies specifically recommends ordinary laundry detergent for machine-washing soft pet items and says it’s okay to wash pet items with your clothes,” says Myers. “For pets described as having sensitive skin, the CDC says detergent without dyes or fragrance may be a good choice.” So if your dog’s skin is easily irritated, a free-and-clear formula, whether or not it’s labeled for pets, may be the better pick.
Frequently asked questions

Pet laundry detergent will work on most of the soft goods your dog uses every day. “Basically, you can use pet laundry detergent on anything belonging to your pet that the manufacturer says can go in the wash, including removable bed covers, blankets, crate pads, towels, washable fabric toys, and pet clothing,” says Myers.
Before you toss something in, check its care label for washing and drying instructions, since some items, like beds with foam inserts, may need to be washed in pieces or by hand.

“Some breeds are more likely to develop allergic and other skin diseases, but that’s not the same thing as certain breeds needing special laundry detergent,” says Myers. That said, Cahn does say that certain breeds have a  higher predisposition to atopic dermatitis and other skin problems, including bulldogs, Boston terriers, boxers, Chinese shar-peis, dalmatians, golden retrievers, labrador retrievers, Lhasa apsos, Scottish terriers, shih tzus, and West Highland white terriers.
“For a dog with diagnosed allergies or otherwise sensitive skin, it is reasonable to choose an unscented, dye-free detergent, and make sure that the laundry is thoroughly rinsed,” says Cahn.

title: Advocates fear deportation of potential witnesses in back of ICE vehicle that hit Houston man
summary: Nidia Delfín said her brother was handcuffed in the back of the ICE vehicle when it hit a man, adding that he has no arrest warrants and that he was getting his green card when he was arrested.
story: HOUSTON — Two handcuffed men were in the backseat of an ICE vehicle Saturday when it struck and injured Miguel Parra Hernandez as he fled on foot in Houston.
Advocates are fighting to make sure the men — now potential witnesses — are not deported.
At a news conference Wednesday, family members, advocates and attorneys identified one of the men as Luis Delfín Enríquez, 48.
Video appears to show Houston man run over by ICE vehicle

Nidia Delfín, Delfín’s sister, said her brother was handcuffed in the backseat of the ICE vehicle when it hit Parra, adding that he was on his way to breakfast with employees when he was apprehended by ICE. She said that Delfín is not a criminal, that he has no arrest warrants and that he was in the process of getting his green card, which means he was on the path to being a legal permanent resident.
“He owns his own small company. He hires people from the community. He is a good man,” she said, adding that he witnessed “this horrific incident.”

She said that she, her parents and her brother are afraid but that they are speaking up so Parra “can get justice.” She pleaded with others in the community who witnessed the incident — she said she has seen videos on social media — to do the same and share the information they have.
“What was done to him is not OK,” she said, referring to Parra. “It’s not how we’re supposed to treat other human beings.”

Cesar Espinosa of FIEL Houston, an immigrant civil rights organization who is representing Parra’s family, said the men held in the ICE vehicle “witnessed everything that happened,” including “the moment when Mr. Miguel [Parra] was run over.”

Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare told NBC News on Tuesday that videos gathered by his office suggest that Parra was struck intentionally. Teare said his office is seeking to interview the witnesses as it investigates the case.
“This was an intentional striking and running over of the person by the vehicle, and in that case, that is an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in Texas,” he said.

A senior Department of Homeland Security official told NBC News on Tuesday that ICE officers on the scene were wearing body cameras and that the agency is reviewing video for an internal investigation.
ICE has said allegations that the agency intentionally struck Parra are “RECKLESS and FALSE.”
Espinosa said that if there is video from body cameras, it should be turned over to the district attorney’s office immediately.

A government watchdog report released Wednesday found that Customs and Border Protection and ICE have not developed specific operational guidance to explain how their personnel should use body cameras.
Without that guidance, “CBP and ICE personnel will fail to use the cameras as required under policy,” the Government Accountability Office said in its report.
The Trump administration issued guidance two weeks ago that dictated that officers on the scenes of vehicle stops must wear and activate their body cameras.

DHS and ICE did not immediately respond to questions about the release of the bodycam video, whether they planned to deport witnesses to the incident and the status of the ICE officer who drove the vehicle that hit Parra.

Security video of the incident obtained by NBC affiliate KPRC of Houston shows a white truck headed in the opposite direction of traffic on a busy roadway. Parra and another man exit the white truck and run, the video shows.
At about the same time, the video shows, another vehicle jumps a yellow median and heads in Parra’s direction.

The video then shows the vehicle, which is not marked, swerving left toward Parra’s path, in front of a truck stopped in a shopping center. When the parked truck leaves, a man can be seen lying on the pavement behind the ICE vehicle, the video shows.
Teare, a Democrat, told NBC News the investigation could lead to charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

Espinosa said at the news conference that Parra does not feel safe at the hospital. The ICE officers who were there when he was struck “are the same crew that are watching him 24/7” at the hospital, Espinosa said. He did not know whether the driver of the vehicle was among those guarding Parra.
ICE did not immediately confirm whether the ICE officers involved in Saturday’s incident are with Parra at the hospital.
Espinosa, Parra’s attorney Kim Bruno and Parra’s family demanded at the news conference that ICE keep Parra at the hospital where he is being treated for his multiple injuries.
Without the proper medical care, he could end up with infections and other problems that could be life-threatening, “so we need him to get the best medical care possible,” Espinosa said.

Espinosa and Bruno said Parra still has not been processed by ICE, which has said that he is in the country illegally. Bruno and Espinosa confirmed that Parra was undocumented and said they could not provide further information about whether he was seeking other status.
Parra, who works applying stucco, has been in the country 34 years, having arrived at age 14, Espinosa and Bruno said.
The man who was driving the truck with Parra and also ran away was identified at the news conference as “Omar.” He does not have a criminal record or any open immigration warrants, Espinosa said.
At the news conference, advocates criticized ICE for pursuing Parra with the immigrants handcuffed in their car, endangering everyone, according to Espinosa.
Teare, who served several years as the chief of the district attorney’s vehicular crimes division, also criticized ICE’s tactics.
“The behavior of this agency and these agents on our streets is so dangerous to everyone that lives in these communities,” he said in an interview Tuesday.
ICE did not immediately respond to allegations that it was conducting an immigration stop while it was transporting immigrants it had previously apprehended.
ICE has said in statements that it was pursuing a man it identified as Jose Mendoza Cervantes, who was in the country illegally and had committed several crimes. It has said Parra was not its target.

Espinosa repeatedly held up a photo of Mendoza at the news conference and said no one, including Parra, recognized him or knew who he was. He also showed a photo of Omar, the man who was with Parra in the car before they fled, to show it was not Mendoza.
“If he [Mendoza] does exist, he must be taken into custody, and a proper thorough investigation must be done so that he may be looked at,” Espinosa said.

title: Kentucky police arrest 8 in child abuse, trafficking and rape case
summary: The seven victims are ages 1 to 17, police in Richmond said.
story: Eight people living in a Kentucky home were arrested in a sweeping child abuse and sexual abuse case involving seven victims, ages 1 to 17, officials said Wednesday.

The suspects face a slew of charges, including abuse, incest, human trafficking and rape. Bail has been set at $50,000 to $125,000, Richmond police spokesperson Makenzie Gould told NBC News in a statement.
All eight defendants are scheduled to appear before a Madison County judge on Oct. 21.
For Subscribers
The arrests followed a joint investigation by Richmond police, Child Protective Services and the Department for Community Based Services, police said in a statement.
“I’m unsure of the exact family relations between all eight members,” Gould said. “All are listed as living at the same residence. All seven children were removed from this same residence.”
For Subscribers
The defendants, along with their ages, charges and bond amounts:
